Noxious Foe is an easy combat achievement which requires the player to kill an aberrant spectre. Killing deviant spectres in the Catacombs of Kourend do not count towards this task.
This achievement requires 60 Slayer to complete. Boosts can be used.
Strategy:
Equipping a nose peg or slayer helmet is required when fighting aberrant spectres. With either of these items equipped, the challenge is as simple as killing any aberrant spectre. Aberrant spectres in the Slayer Tower can be killed regardless of whether or not you are on task, whilst the ones in the Stronghold Slayer Cave cannot be killed unless on an aberrant spectre Slayer task. With 67 Sailing, the aberrant spectres on Deepfin Point can be killed without a slayer task. Notably, this location is the only place where skillers can obtain this combat achievement.

They Grow Up Too Fast is a hard combat achievement requiring the player to kill the Abyssal Sire before any spawns mature into a scion.
Strategy:
This is considered one of the more difficult of the hard combat achievements.
Spawns can appear during each phase of the fight, have 15 hitpoints and mature after 12 seconds. These will appear throughout the fight.
In phase 1, spawns will appear if the Sire is within attack range (~10 spaces), though it tends to frequently launch miasma pools. This should not be an issue as players should be using shadow spells to disorient it, and will mostly remain outside of this range.
In phase 2, spawns will appear rather infrequently, but will have a much greater chance of being launched if the player is out of melee distance. As such, stay within melee distance to minimise the chances of spawns appearing. At this stage or before the end of phase 3, it may be beneficial to use Emberlight or Bandos godsword special attacks to drain the Sire's defence, to reduce the chance of attacks missing before he can be killed.
In phase 3, part 1, four spawns will appear immediately once the Sire roots itself to the ground and becomes attackable again. These spawns must be killed immediately, and can be stacked by moving a few tiles back. After these spawns are killed, the player can take a short breather, as no further spawns will appear until the next part begins.
(More on the wiki page of this task.)

Respiratory Runner is an elite combat achievement which requires the player to kill the Abyssal Sire after only stunning him once.
This task fails whenever Sire wakes up from a stun; killing the respiratory systems via safespotting or tanking the tentacles must be done before stunning Sire. Likewise, enough damage to the Sire must be dealt or a shadow spell cast to disorient it exactly once.
Leaving the nexus will fail the achievement attempt unless you don't wake up the Sire.
Strategy:
The scorching bow trivialises this achievement, as it will always kill the respiratory systems in one shot, regardless of Ranged accuracy and ammo used.
For players without a scorching bow, note that upon a successful hit, players will always hit at least 50% of their maximum hit on the systems, meaning a setup with a maximum hit close to 50 will always kill the systems in 2 shots. Additionally, the bonuses from a Slayer helm apply to the respiratory systems. With high levels in either Magic or Ranged and late-game gear (such as a bow of Faerdhinen and full crystal armour), it is possible to kill all four in a single stun, but it will require minimising the time taken to travel between systems, such as running to the next system immediately after the player receives an experience drop that confirms they killed the previous system.
(More on the wiki page of this task.)

Don't Whip Me is a hard combat achievement which requires the player to kill the Abyssal Sire without being hit by any external tentacles.\nThis achievement is easily obtained by only attacking the vents after having successfully disoriented the Abyssal Sire with a shadow spell, preferably Shadow Barrage as it is 100% effective. Once the Abyssal Sire roots itself after having reached 200 HP, the player should only stay in the three centremost rows of squares to avoid any damage from the tentacles.

Demonic Rebound is an elite combat achievement requiring the player to use Vengeance against the Abyssal Sire's explosion attack.
Strategy:
In order to cast shadow spells to disorient the Sire, the player must use Spellbook Swap to swap to the Ancient spellbook. The explosion attack can deal up to 96 damage, so it is highly recommended to have as many Hitpoints as possible and boost it with a Saradomin brew or Anglerfish. It is also recommended to kill the four spawns that appear when the Sire roots itself to avoid having them waste Vengeance.
Staying alive is not required for successfully completing the achievement, so you can also try this without a lot of health.
Another account can also cast Vengeance Other on you, and it will count toward this combat achievement, eliminating the need for a way to change spellbooks. The other account does not have to be on an Abyssal demon Slayer task to do this.
Since the fight does not stop if you teleport out, another strategy is to start the fight with the Ancient spellbook, kill the scions at the beginning of phase 3, teleport out, switch to the Lunar spellbook, come back and cast the vengeance. It is recommended that you have a Lunar Altar in your POH if doing this strategy, since taking too long to come back can make the fight reset.

Don't Stop Moving is a hard combat achievement which requires the player to kill the Abyssal Sire without taking damage from any miasma pools.
Strategy:
Miasma pools have a one second delay before they damage the player and have a 3x3 AoE from their initial spawn point. They will disappear after a few seconds.
During phase 3, the player should trigger the pool on a location other than the south-west safe tile prior to starting the next stage when the Sire falls below 140 health, as it will perform its explosion attack once this threshold is triggered. While the player is safe from damage for a few seconds, it also locks them in place slightly longer, which could result in damage from a pool.

Collateral Damage is a master combat achievement which requires the player to kill Kree'arra in a private instance without ever attacking him directly.\nStrategy:\nThis can be achieved with chinchompas easily. Recoil damage through Vengeance, especially enhanced with Dharok the Wretched's equipment with amulet of the damned, ring of suffering, and barrage spells may also be used, but they are less effective overall. Beware that simply targeting Kree'arra, even while on attack cooldown, to prevent him from using his melee attack will automatically fail the task.

Airborne Showdown is a hard combat achievement which requires the player to finish off Kree'arra whilst all of his bodyguards are dead.\nStrategy:\nA good method to complete this task solo, alongside the similar tasks for each of the respective God Wars Dungeon bosses, is to use a Toxic blowpipe alongside a Serpentine helm to envenom the bodyguards between kills, so that when the boss is low on health all of the minions are also low/dead, allowing them to be killed easier.

Swoop No More is a master combat achievement which requires the player to kill Kree'arra in a private instance without taking any melee damage from the boss or his bodyguards.
Strategy:
Although killing Kree'arra using Protect from Melee would complete this task, Kree'arra consistently hits high damage with ranged so this is not recommended.
Kree'arra only closes in for melee attacks if he is not presently targeted, so if distance is maintained while using Protect from Missiles, the only threat for melee damage will be Flight Kilisa. Flight Kilisa only has level 50 Magic and no magic defence, so she can be bound with magic fairly reliably.
If you're having trouble binding Flight Kilisa, it's possible to toggle Protect from Melee only while Flight Kilisa is alive and killing her by immediately stepping under Kree'arra. Once Flight Kilisa dies, quickly turn your prayers back to Protect from Missiles and Rigour and step out of Kree'arra to damage him. Repeat the previous process when Flight Kilisa respawns, 2 or 3 repetitions should be enough to complete the combat achievement. Tagging Flight Kilisa and Kree'arra using RuneLite makes this process easier by showing you their tiles and helping you quickly noticing respawns.
Alternatively, players will usually complete this task passively by the time they get to 100 kills, as long as Kree'arra is fought in a private instance each time.
(More on the wiki page of this task.)

The Worst Ranged Weapon is a grandmaster combat achievement which requires the player to kill Kree'arra via damage inflicted by salamanders.
Strategy:
The tecu salamander is recommended, as it is the strongest salamander available, requiring irit tar as ammo and level 80 Attack, Ranged, and Magic to use. Players should use the salamander in melee mode, as it hits significantly harder than ranged and Kree'arra has slightly less melee defence compared to ranged.
It is also very recommended to bring a mix of strong defensive equipment with high defence bonuses in all three styles, while also trying to maximise strength and slash bonuses, as Ranged accuracy will only be around 20% with a salamander. Oathplate armour and the bellator ring should be used over other options in order to increase slash accuracy.
The inventory should consist of about 200 irit tars, multiple super combat potions, a crossbow and grapple, and as many Saradomin brews and super restores as possible.
Players should keep Protect from Missiles and Piety on at all times. It is also advised to walk under Kree'arra after every attack to minimise his overall attacks, as he has an attack speed of 3, whereas the salamanders have an attack speed of 5 when used on the scorch (melee) style.
With an aviansie slayer task, using a slayer helmet will make the achievement much easier.
(More on the wiki page of this task.)

Feather Hunter is a grandmaster Combat Achievement which requires the player to kill Kree'arra 30 times in a private instance without leaving the room.
Strategy:
It is recommended to use either a Tumeken's shadow or the chinchompa method. Having an aviansies slayer task will be a huge benefit. Kree is the only God Wars Dungeon boss not to drop any prayer restoration, so players will need to bring at least eight prayer potions/prayer regeneration potions. Expect the achievement to take around 65 minutes.
First, pre-pot with an anglerfish and a super defence potion.
If using a Tumeken's shadow, also bring runes for blood barrage and bones to peaches tabs; optionally take an eldritch Nightmare staff and ice barrage. Start each kill in the south-west corner of the room and freeze Flight Kilisa whenever possible (or alternatively step under Kree after each attack). If you need to heal during a kill, step under Kree. Once Kree dies, blood barrage both Kilisa and Flockleader Geerin to restore any lost health and use the eldritch staff's special attack on Skree to restore prayer. Bring bones to peaches tabs, as the resulting peaches will restore 32 health per spawn cycle.
(More on the wiki page of this task.)

Ourg Freezer is a hard combat achievement which requires the player to kill General Graardor while he is immobilised. The task will be completed if the final attack would have immobilised Graardor.\nStrategy:\nFor the purposes of this task, bind spells from the standard spellbook or ice spells from the ancient spellbook are recommended. The Zamorak godsword could also be used for this task, although if the player is aiming for Ourg Freezer II, it is recommended to use ice spells to complete both achievements at once.

Ourg Freezer II is an elite combat achievement which requires the player to kill General Graardor without him attacking any players.
Strategy:
This achievement is best combined with Ourg Freezer, as the player has to bind Graardor to kill him anyway.
Alternatively, the Ranged method using an Armadyl crossbow or Bow of Faerdhinen will complete this task if performed flawlessly. This option will not complete Ourg Freezer.

General Showdown is a hard combat achievement which requires the player to finish off General Graardor whilst all of his bodyguards are dead.\nStrategy:\nA good method to complete this task solo, alongside the similar tasks for each of the respective God Wars Dungeon bosses, is to use a Toxic blowpipe alongside a Serpentine helm to envenom the bodyguards between kills, so that when the boss is low on health all of the minions are also low/dead, allowing them to be killed easier.

Defence Matters is a grandmaster combat achievement which requires the player to kill General Graardor two consecutive times in one trip in a private instance without taking damage from his bodyguards.
Strategy:
Prayer Flick Method
Prayer flick the bodyguards' attacks; ideally try to make Sergeant Strongstack hit on the same tick as Graardor so both attacks are blocked. Make sure that Sergeant Steelwill and Sergeant Grimspike also attack on different ticks. Graardor has an attack speed of 6 (3.6s) while the bodyguards have an attack speed of 5 (3.0s). Walking under Graardor can help resync off-ticks.
An adaptation that might be easier but requires extended focus is to keep the minions alive after killing Graardor once, then focus on flicking them correctly without killing them as Graardor respawns. By wearing powerful defensive armour such as Justiciar armour or Torva armour, and using an Osmumten's fang with a strong shield such as the elysian spirit shield or dragonfire shield, it should be possible to tank and kill Graardor twice with a decent amount of healing supplies.
Players with knowledge of the 5:0 Tumeken's shadow strategy may opt to do a modified version of it for the achievement:
- Kill Graardor normally, then kill Strongstack and Grimspike.
(More on the wiki page of this task.)

Keep Away is a grandmaster combat achievement which requires the player to kill General Graardor in an instance without taking any damage from him or his bodyguards.
Strategy:
This achievement requires Ranged or Magic in order to complete, since Graardor's melee attacks are accurate even with best-in-slot melee armour. Use Ice Barrage and the best magic equipment available to quickly kill Graardor, or try to flick the minions while using one of the methods that prevents Graardor from attacking (e.g., 5:0 with a Tumeken's shadow). Freezing Sergeant Strongstack is helpful but not needed, since he will usually be trailing with Graardor.
Make sure that both Sergeant Grimspike and Sergeant Steelwill are attacking on different ticks, so their attacks can be flicked against, since both are fairly accurate even with good defensive bonuses.
One method that can be used to make this achievement easier is to keep the minions alive but at low health after killing Graardor. Just as Graardor respawns, kill whatever spawns closest to the player's position, then freeze Sergeant Grimspike in a good location so the remaining long-ranged minion has to be prayed against. If the kill seems to be dragging on, the remaining minion can be killed before the other long-ranged minion respawns.

Ourg Killer is a grandmaster combat achievement which requires the player to kill General Graardor 15 times in a private instance without leaving the room.
In order to rent a private instance, the player must have the Hard Combat Achievements completed.
Strategy:
Using either the magic freezing method, ranged method or even just face-tanking with an elysian spirit shield and Justiciar armour, this task can easily be completed with very little prior experience in fighting General Graardor. If melee is being used, flicking the mage minion every other attack, might increase chances for success. Since General Graardor drops super restores relatively commonly, having a little bit of luck should be enough to complete this task without much practice.

Barrows Novice is an easy combat achievement which requires the player to open the Barrows chest 10 times.
Completion of the quest Priest in Peril is required to complete this task, as this quest is required to enter Morytania.
Strategy:
This combat achievement can be finished quickly by running through the barrows and finding out which sarcophagus enters into the tunnel, disregarding any brother that appears. This method yields around 30-50 chest openings per hour. Note that almost no loot will be received using this method. It is the fastest way to get killcount, however. With the Strange old lockpick, players can ignore the random path and head straight into the middle room, making trips faster at the cost of a charge when passing through a locked door.

Barrows Champion is a medium combat achievement which requires the player to open the Barrows chest 25 times.\nStrategy:\nThis combat achievement can be finished quickly by running through the barrows and finding out which sarcophagus enters into the tunnel, disregarding any brother that appears. This method yields around 30-50 chest openings per hour. Note that almost no loot will be received using this method. It is the fastest way to get killcount, however. With the Strange old lockpick, players can ignore the random path and head straight into the middle room, making trips faster at the cost of a charge when passing through a locked door.

Can't Touch Me is a medium combat achievement which requires the player to kill Dharok, Verac, Torag, and Guthan without letting them attack the player with melee. Using Protect from Melee to block damage will not count.
If you have killed 0 of the brothers and get hit by the first brother you try to kill, leaving and re-entering the crypt will NOT reset the task, so you will need to open the chest and start over.
After killing the 4 brothers without being hit, the combat achievement will not unlock until after opening the chest.
Strategy:
To complete this task, it is recommended to keep doing Barrows runs, starting with Ahrim and Karil, until one of these two is in the entrance to the tunnels. After that, the exact same strategy can be applied to all four remaining brothers. For these melee brothers, the general strategy is to search the coffin and then immediately run to the opposite side of their coffin. Due to the small delay before a brother attacks, it is even possible to run through the brother when running to the other side of the coffin. The special attack of a dragon spear can be used to stun the brothers should this prove difficult.
Turn off run energy, and cast the best freezing spell available, such as Ice spells or Entangle. Then immediately run back, in case the freeze splashes.
(More on the wiki page of this task.)

Pray for Success is a medium combat achievement which requires the player to kill all six Barrows Brothers and loot the Barrows chest without taking any damage from any of the brothers.
Strategy:
As the name suggests, the task is easiest completed by using protection prayers during the fights.
Using Protect from Magic when fighting Ahrim the Blighted, Protect from missiles when fighting Karil the Tainted, and Protect from Melee when fighting Dharok the Wretched, Guthan the Infested, Torag the Corrupted and Verac the Defiled. It is however possible for Verac to hit through Protect from Melee, thus players should consider binding him with binding spells like Entangle or ice spells to minimise the chance of him landing a damaging hit. When spawning Verac, use a Dragon spear special attack to stun him or immediately run behind the coffin to avoid getting hit.
Once the player has taken damage from a brother, the chest must be found and looted before another attempt is made. This applies even to the first brother fought; leaving the room to reset the fight does not allow this task to be completed even if all six brothers are subsequently killed without damaging the player.
Players should also take the prayer-drain effect in the Barrows into consideration and bring some means of prayer restoration like Prayer potions.

Defence? What Defence? is an easy combat achievement which requires the player to kill any Barrows brother using only magic damage.
Completion of the quest Priest in Peril is required to complete this task, as this quest is required to enter Morytania.
Strategy:
Dharok the Wretched and Guthan the Infested both have negative magic defence. Torag the Corrupted and Verac the Defiled are also very vulnerable to magic attacks. Killing these brothers with magic is highly advisable, so completing this task is in line with the recommended strategy for killing the Barrows Brothers.

Just Like That is a hard combat achievement which requires the player to kill Karil the Tainted using only damage dealt by special attacks.
Strategy:
Using a lightbearer is recommended. Players can also have a friend cast Energy Transfer on them to restore their special attack energy for this achievement, or wait in a safespot for their special attack energy to naturally recover. Poison damage (from a Dragon dagger p++ for example), venom damage, as well as a charged Dragonfire Shield attack may be utilised. The burn from burning claws or the Arkan blade will fail this achievement.
For lower levels, or Ironmen, the rune thrownaxe delivers moderate, reliable damage for only 10% special attack energy per throw. Players should turn off auto-retaliate and click away after each throw as the rune thrownaxe has a relatively fast attack speed and it is easy to accidentally auto-attack Karil.
Normal attacks that do not deal damage do not count against this combat achievement.

Faithless Crypt Run is a hard combat achievement which requires the player to kill all six Barrows Brothers and loot the Barrows chest without ever having more than 0 Prayer points.
Strategy:
If the player enters the first coffin room with any amount of prayer points, it will not count, even if all prayer points are drained before summoning the first brother.
The melee brothers can be frozen to reduce the amount of damage taken, leaving only Karil and Ahrim able to damage the player.
Note that the player cannot hop worlds when doing this achievement, as it checks both digging to enter the crypt, and the kill itself.
If the player dies while attempting this achievement, their stat reset on respawn will result in more than 0 prayer, causing the achievement to fail.

Reflecting on This Encounter is an elite combat achievement which requires the player to kill a basilisk knight. Basilisk knights are only found in the Jormungand's Prison on the Island of Stone. In order to access the dungeon, the quest Fremennik Exiles must be completed.

Big, Black and Fiery is an easy combat achievement which requires the player to kill a black dragon. While the King Black Dragon and brutal black dragons count towards this task, baby black dragons do not.\nStrategy:\nIt is recommended to kill the King Black Dragon because it is part of another easy combat achievement, King Black Dragon Novice, to progress in two at once. Players with level 77 Slayer may also opt to kill a brutal black dragon to complete medium task Brutal, Big, Black and Firey at the same time.

The Demonic Punching Bag is an easy combat achievement which requires the player to kill a bloodveld or Mutated Bloodveld.
A Slayer level of 50 is required to damage bloodvelds. Boosts can be used.
Strategy:
Bloodvelds require no specific equipment to be killed, but as their attacks are magic-based melee attacks, it is advisable to bring dragonhide gear if the player's combat stats are low. The bloodvelds in the Stronghold Slayer Cave and Morytania Slayer Tower basement can only be hurt while on Slayer task, so unless the player's task is to kill bloodveld, another location has to be chosen.
Brutal, Big, Black and Firey is a medium combat achievement which requires the player to kill a brutal black dragon. A Slayer level of 77 is required to damage a brutal black dragon.
Bryophyta Novice is an easy combat achievement which requires the player to kill Bryophyta and loot her chest with a mossy key once. The regular strategies can be followed to complete this task.

Protection from Moss is an easy combat achievement which requires the player to kill Bryophyta with the Protect from Magic prayer active.
To activate the Protect from Magic prayer, a Prayer level of 37 is required. Boosts will not work.
Strategy:
The prayer doesn't have to be used throughout the fight, but it has to be active when Bryophyta finishes her death animation and the loot appears on the ground.

Quick Cutter is a medium combat achievement which requires the player to kill all 3 of Bryophyta's growthlings within 3 seconds of the first one dying.
Strategy:
To kill the growthlings, make all three of them stand directly adjacent to the player, then wield magic secateurs or an axe and attack all three in quick succession.
With sufficient food and/or prayer points, this achievement can be attempted multiple times during the same fight with Bryophyta.

Preparation Is Key is an easy combat achievement which requires the player to kill Bryophyta without suffering any poison damage.
Strategy:
Bryophyta does not poison on free-to-play worlds, so killing her on a free-to-play world will automatically complete this task. This will also complete the Fighting as Intended II task.
Alternatively, if the player wishes to do this task on a members world, they can choose to bring an antipoison potion or protect from poison in another way.

A Slow Death is an easy combat achievement which requires the player to kill Bryophyta with either poison or venom being the final source of damage.\nStrategy:\nPlayers can wear a serpentine helm alongside a toxic blowpipe or trident of the swamp to guarantee that Bryophyta is inflicted with venom on the next successful hit, attack her until her health is low, and then wait for the venom to take effect. Alternatively, any poison weapon can be used to apply regular poison. If the player's combat stats are low, make sure to bring some extra supplies to outlast any extra attacks Bryophyta might inflict while waiting for the venom or poison to take effect.

Fighting as Intended II is an easy combat achievement which requires the player to kill Bryophyta on a free to play world.
Strategy:
Suggested Skills:
- Level 37 Prayer or higher for the Protect from Magic prayer
- If using Melee:
- Level 50 Attack or higher
- Level 50 Strength or higher
- Level 50 Defence or higher
- If using Ranged:
- Level 60 Ranged or higher
- Level 40 Defence or higher
- If using Magic:
- Level 59 Magic for Fire Blast or 35 Magic for Fire Bolt
- Level 40 Defence or higher
Equipment:
Melee=
|-|
Ranged=
In order to reach Bryophyta, players will need a knife or slash weapon to slash the web to get to the lair if they are reaching her via the Varrock Sewers. Members with level 51 Agility do not need this as they can access an agility shortcut by Vannaka in the Edgeville Dungeon before switching to a free-to-play world. Members may also use a Giantsoul amulet to teleport directly to the lair.
Unlike Obor's chambers (where he is confined in a small pit), players are immediately taken to Bryophyta's chambers, where she will attack them on sight - prior to entering the room, or immediately after entering, activate Protect from Magic.
During the fight, she may summon three growthlings - they are fairly weak, but they must be killed, as Bryophyta is immune to all damage while they are alive.
(More on the wiki page of this task.)
Callisto Adept is a hard combat achievement which requires the player to kill Callisto 10 times. Both Callisto and his singles-plus variant Artio kills count towards this task.
Callisto Veteran is an elite combat achievement which requires the player to kill Callisto 20 times. Both Callisto and his singles-plus variant Artio kills count towards this task.

Demonic Weakening is a medium combat achievement requiring the player to kill Skotizo with no altars active.
Strategy:
Altars that activate after Skotizo is killed do not fail the task. However, altars can activate immediately before the kill, failing the task. Minimise this chance by verifying they are all down while dealing the last blow.
When an altar is destroyed, there is a one minute cooldown before that altar can re-activate again. By letting all altars activate and then quickly destroying them, you can then safely finish off Skotizo with no risk of the altars reactivating.

Demon Evasion is an elite combat achievement which requires the player to kill Skotizo without taking any damage.
Strategy:
In order to not take any damage the player must pray Protect from Magic and stay out of melee distance from Skotizo, the three reanimated demon spawns, and the dark ankou. The dark ankou will only start following the player if the player gets too close. Using a ranged weapon with a high attack range will make it easier to keep distance from the enemies while running. Take Arclight or Emberlight to quickly kill the Awakened Altars. Multi-target binds such as ice burst or ice barrage can be cast when the 3 demon spawns are grouped together in order to freeze them and allow the player to briefly stop and attack Skotizo. Since this achievement requires a lot of running, several stamina potions should be taken. The self-damaging effects of ruby dragon bolts (e), ruby bolts (e), and divine potions will not cause the achievement to fail.
When the reanimated demon spawns are following you in a line, you can also bind the first one in the line which stops them all as they cannot go through each other. They can go through Skotizo, however. You will still need to deal with the reanimated demon spawns as they will still spawn after 3 minutes. Killing two of the reanimated demon spawns also prevents re-spawning them, so you only have to kite one of them.
(More on the wiki page of this task.)

Demonbane Weaponry is a medium combat achievement which requires the player to kill Skotizo with a demonbane weapon equipped.\nHoly water does not count as a demonbane weapon for the purpose of this achievement.

Up for the Challenge is an elite combat achievement which requires the player to kill Skotizo, or Awakened Altars without equipping a demonbane weapon.
Strategy:
The most effective way to complete this achievement is to use the twisted bow, for its increased power and accuracy against monsters with high Magic bonuses, such as Skotizo. Players who do not own a twisted bow may instead opt to use regular melee attacks.
While this task prohibits equipping the Silverlight, Darklight, Arclight, Emberlight, Scorching bow or Burning Claws, it does not prohibit casting Demonbane spells, since those are not equipped weapons. Additionally, Purging staff and Holy water are not considered to be demonbane weapons for this task.
The hardest part of this challenge is keeping the number of altars down to one or zero. However, with sufficient stats and gear it can be navigated without too much difficulty, as the awakened altars have a cooldown of one minute once destroyed before they can reactivate.
Some tips: Death charge does NOT work on the awakened altars. Greater corruption can be valuable when attacking Skotizo. Having a demonbane weapon in the inventory to finish him off if you fail does not fail the challenge so can be worth it.
(More on the wiki page of this task.)

Precise Positioning is a master combat achievement which requires the player to kill Skotizo with the final source of damage being a chinchompa explosion.
It is possible to complete this achievement and Demonbane Weaponry on the same kill by equipping a demonbane weapon after throwing the chinchompa that deals the finishing blow but before Skotizo takes damage from the explosion.
Strategy:
The attack must not be targeted against Skotizo directly, but must be collateral damage from a reanimated demon spawn or dark ankou that is underneath or directly adjacent to Skotizo's south-west tile. This is because Skotizo is larger than 1x1 so it will only receive collateral damage from area-of-effect attacks that hit its south-western tile.
The Scorching bow's special attack, Scorching shackles, will bind Skotizo in place for 20 ticks(12 seconds). This can aid in positioning Skotizo to easily receive collateral damage from the reanimated demon spawn or dark ankou, but be careful that the burn damage does not accidentally deal the finishing blow.

Arooo No More is a master combat achievement which requires the player to kill Cerberus without her summoning any Summoned Souls during the battle.
Strategy:
Cerberus summons souls every 7 attacks from the start of her attack rotation, but only when below 400 health. With an attack speed of 6, or 3.6 seconds between attacks, she must be flinched and walked under in order to obtain the achievement; otherwise there won't be enough time to kill her within seven attacks.
Alternatively, the player can wait for Cerberus to attack 14 times before dropping her below 400 health, as the souls only appear when she falls below that threshold. The next occurrence of this attack, attack 21, is overridden by her triple attack, which occurs every ten attacks from the first. This means that the player has ~46.8 seconds to defeat Cerberus before the next set of souls appears with minimal walking. With maximum flinching and walking, additional time can be provided at the start of the encounter.
Cerberus has a 10% chance to use a standard attack instead of summoning souls on her 7th attack, so if the player is able to consistently complete the kill before her 14th attack, eventually, this achievement will be completed passively.
See the Dharok's armour 'red-click' strategy for an additional method of completing this combat achievement.

Ghost Buster is an elite combat achievement which requires the player to kill Cerberus after successfully negating 6 or more attacks from Summoned Souls.\nThis task counts attacks from each individual Summoned Soul, so negating two sets of three is sufficient to complete this achievement.

Unrequired Antifire is an elite combat achievement which requires the player to kill Cerberus without taking any damage from her lava pool attacks.
Strategy:
The lava pool attack is indicated when Cerberus growls "Grrrr", launching three markers around the arena - one on the player's position at the time the mechanic was initiated, and two around it. It is recommended to use Ranged when attempting this achievement as the markers have a delay when launched at a distance, allowing the player to quickly move out of the way. This attack is initiated when Cerberus falls below 200 health and is performed on every attack that ends in 0 or 5 on her attack rotation.
Alternatively, the player can simply kill Cerberus before she has a chance to use the mechanic.

Anti-Bite Mechanics is an elite combat achievement which requires the player to kill Cerberus without taking any melee damage.\nStrategy:\nThis achievement is best done with Ranged as Cerberus does not actively move in to attack the player with melee. This leaves her triple combo attack as the only threat, as the last hit deals melee damage and does not take distance into account.

Hoarder is a hard combat achievement which requires the player to kill the Chaos Elemental without it unequipping any of their items.
Much like The Flincher, if any player has their equipment unequipped, everyone involved in the kill will fail.
Strategy:
The Chaos Elemental cannot unequip items as long as the player does not have the required inventory space for them to be unequipped. Because of this, it is recommended to bring pies, stews, or curry as food, as they will leave behind a pie dish or bowl upon being eaten. Alternatively, Saradomin brews can be brought instead, as long as the "smash vials" ability is not activated. Note that Saradomin brews drain stats so bringing super restores would be advisable.
Failure only occurs if a player has an item removed from their equipment slots from the madness projectile. If the player hit by the projectile does not have anything equipped, the combat task is still achievable. This can be used with the Solo Safe Spot Method to guarantee task completion if the luring is done without any items equipped, even if there are slots available in the inventory.

The Flincher is a hard combat achievement which requires the player to kill the Chaos Elemental without taking any damage from its attacks.
If any player takes damage from its attacks, everyone involved in the kill will fail.
Strategy:
Given that the Chaos Elemental has a very long range and its attacks dealing either magic, ranged or melee damage with no distinction, it is quite difficult to draw its attention without getting hit. Attacking with a 10-square attack range weapon while the Chaos Elemental is not facing the player and quickly running behind a safespot is an effective way to achieve this.
Wearing a full set of Verac the Defiled's equipment with the Protect Item prayer turned on is an excellent way to complete the achievement, since the full set allows players to bypass the Chaos Elemental's defences. Praying Protect from Magic, the player should try to get the attention of the elemental, with a little luck, they should take no damage from potential ranged or melee attacks, whilst luring the Chaos Elemental towards the small trees outside the Rogues' Castle walls. When the Chaos Elemental is in place, the player should start flinching it by attacking the elemental once, then immediately step back behind the tree, then wait for the elemental's HP bar to disappear before landing the next attack. This should ensure that the Chaos Elemental has no chance to retaliate.
(More on the wiki page of this task.)
Sorry, What Was That? is a medium combat achievement which requires the player to kill the Chaos Fanatic without anyone being hit by his explosion attack.

Praying to the Gods is a hard combat achievement which requires the player to kill the Chaos Fanatic 10 times, without drinking any potion which restores prayer, or leaving the Wilderness.
Warning: Entering Ferox Enclave will reset the kill count for this combat task. Even though it is technically in the Wilderness, it is not considered wilderness for the purpose of this task. In general, only places where you risk losing items count.
The altar east of Ferox can be used to recharge prayer, or the Chaos Altar for a closer and more dangerous method.
Strategy:
This task prohibits the consumption of only the following items:
- Prayer potion
- Prayer regeneration potion (Consuming this will reset the task, but you are allowed to have the regeneration effect active while getting kills)
- Zamorak brew
- Super restore
- Sanfew serum
- Ancient brew
- Moonlight moth mix
- Stat Restore Pot Share of any of the above
This means it is allowed to make use of several other prayer-restoring items, which notably includes the Falador shields, and Moonlight moths (non-mix version). Jangerberries, Bluefin, yellow spicy stew, and another player sharing a Moonlight moth mix can also be used, however these items are not recommended for practical use.
(More on the wiki page of this task.)

Hot on Your Feet is an elite combat achievement which requires the player to kill the Corporeal Beast without killing or taking damage from the dark energy core.
Strategy:
This can be accomplished by moving 2 tiles whenever the dark energy core jumps towards the player. Solo players should not bring a cannon as it will end up killing the core.
If the core would have damaged the player but the damage is nulled through teleporting, the achievement is still failed, and no failure message is received.
If teleporting out of the room mid kill, it is recommended to move away from the core first or to time the teleport such that the core could not have damaged the player throughout the length of the teleport animation.

Finding the Weak Spot is an elite combat achievement which requires the player to finish off the Corporeal Beast with a dragon halberd or crystal halberd special attack.\nFor this task to completed successfully, the halberd has to be using the stab attack style.

Chicken Killer is an elite combat achievement which requires the player to kill the Corporeal Beast alone.\nStrategy:\nFor non-ironmen players, it is recommended to complete the achievement using an instance - while this will cost money and requires another player to hold the instance, the Corporeal Beast has a lot of health and the player might get crashed by other players, particularly griefers, while attempting the task. Ironmen players do not have to worry as much as they get their own room if they have a combat level of 90 or higher, although the room is still shared on that world with all other ironmen.

Mage of the Ruins is a medium combat achievement which requires the player to kill the Crazy Archaeologist with only magical attacks.\nDamage inflicted by a ring of recoil or by the special attack of a dragonfire shield also counts as magical for the purpose of this task.

If Gorillas Could Fly is an elite combat achievement which requires the player to kill a demonic gorilla.\nStrategy:\nThis task can be completed during the Monkey Madness II quest by damaging a demonic gorilla and having Nieve finish it off. Alternatively, demonic gorillas can be found in the Crash Site Cavern after completing Monkey Madness II.

Hitting Them Where It Hurts is an elite combat achievement which requires the player to finish off a demonic gorilla with a demonbane weapon.\nStrategy:\nThis task can be completed very easily by using Arclight or Emberlight, and any of the demonbane spells with or without a purging staff, as both are easily accessible and ensures the gorilla can be dealt the last blow with a demonbane weapon regardless of what it prays against. If using Ranged instead of Magic, it is possible that the last blow on the gorilla has to be done with a ranged weapon, in which case the scorching bow may be used instead. If the player does not have either the bow or demonbane spells, killing just a few will likely result in being able to kill one with melee as the last attack style.

Mage of the Swamp is a medium combat achievement which requires the player to kill the Deranged Archaeologist with only magical attacks.\nDamage inflicted by a ring of recoil or by the special attack of a dragonfire shield also counts as magical for the purpose of this task.

I'd Rather Be Illiterate is a medium combat achievement which requires the player to kill the Deranged Archaeologist without anyone being hit by his "Learn to Read" attack.\nStrategy:\nThe easiest way to get this achievement is simply to choose two points in the boss area to run between special attacks. Whenever he shouts "Learn to Read!", run to the opposite point in the area. While it is possible to get unlucky and be hit by one of the smaller books, there's a good chance that the attack will be avoided entirely by giving a wide enough berth.

The Walking Volcano is an easy combat achievement which requires the player to kill a fire giant.
Strategy:
Fire giants are very easy to kill for low-level players with fairly decent food and equipment. Players with a Prayer level of at least 43 can utilise Protect from Melee to negate all damage given from them.
Fire giants have a significant elemental weakness to water spells. Players may also opt to safespot them with magic. There are many areas with fire giants that include convenient safespots, such as the Brimhaven Dungeon, Stronghold Slayer Cave, and Waterfall Dungeon.
If all easy combat achievements are planned to be completed, it is efficient to kill a fire giant, moss giant, and a hill giant in the Giants' Den within the Shayzien region to complete this achievement and Into the Den of Giants at the same time.

Galvek Speed-Trialist is an elite combat achievement which requires the player to kill Galvek in less than 3 minutes. The fight can be attempted at the Pool of Dreams to the east on the Myths' Guild's .
The player must deal 1200 damage to Galvek in 300 ticks, or 49 possible Dragon hunter crossbow (Rapid) attacks averaging 24.48 damage per attack.
Strategy:
The recommended strategy is to use a dragon crossbow (or better) with ruby dragon bolts (e), and a strong special attack weapon, such as a zaryte crossbow, voidwaker, or burning claws. As Galvek's defence resets between phases, defence reduction is generally less effective here. For players with weaker range equipment, using a strong melee weapon such as Osmumten's fang or a Dragon hunter lance for Galvek's final phase might be more effective.
For highest odds of successful completion, start the Galvek fight and instantly start clicking on where his character will spawn during the dark transition screen. If the ruby bolts do not activate their special effect on the first attack, teleport back to the Myths' Guild with the mythical cape and restart. When the ruby bolt special is activated on the first attack, prepare for an attempt at the goal time. Use any special attacks immediately, and continue to range Galvek.
- Food such as Guthix rests or Saradomin brews will avoid losing ticks
(More on the wiki page of this task.)

Perfect Grotesque Guardians is an elite combat achievement which requires the player to kill the Grotesque Guardians whilst completing the Don't Look at the Eclipse, Prison Break, Granite Footwork, Heal No More, Static Awareness, and Done before Dusk tasks.
This means the player must kill the Grotesque Guardians without doing the following:
- Taking damage from Dusk's blinding attack.
- Taking damage from Dusk's prison attack.
- Taking damage from Dawn's rockfall attack.
- Letting Dawn receive any healing from her orbs.
- Being hit by any lightning attacks.
- Letting Dusk use his prison attack for a second time.

Perfect Grotesque Guardians II is a master combat achievement which requires the player to kill the Grotesque Guardians five times in a row without leaving the area, whilst satisfying the conditions for Perfect Grotesque Guardians.
This means the player must avoid the following:
- Taking damage from Dusk's blinding attack.
- Taking damage from Dusk's prison attack.
- Taking damage from Dawn's rockfall attack.
- Letting Dawn receive any healing from her orbs.
- Being hit by any lightning attacks.
- Letting Dusk use his prison attack for a second time.
- Leaving the instance.
Strategy:
The hardest part of this achievement is avoiding the lightning attacks that come after reducing Dusk's health below half. To avoid the attacks, it is recommended to stay still on a tile and have run turned on, so that one can escape to two tiles away in a single tick if needed. If the player is using special attacks such as that of the crystal halberd or dragon claws, it is recommended to use these on the final phase of the fight, as not killing Dusk in time will allow him to use a second prison attack. Being trampled by Dusk does not fail the achievement.

Grotesque Guardians Speed-Trialist is an elite combat achievement which requires the player to kill the Grotesque Guardians in 2:00 or less. Despite the official description, a time of exactly 2:00.00 will count for the achievement.\nStrategy:\nFor strategies on this achievement, see Grotesque Guardians Speed-Runner.

Grotesque Guardians Speed-Chaser is a master combat achievement which requires the player to kill the Grotesque Guardians in under 1 minute and 40 seconds.\nStrategy:\nFor strategies on this achievement, see Grotesque Guardians Speed-Runner.

Grotesque Guardians Speed-Runner is a grandmaster combat achievement which requires the player to kill the Grotesque Guardians in less than 1 minute and 20 seconds.
Strategy:
Players have two options for this achievement; pure melee, or a melee/ranged hybrid.
As hybrid, players are recommended to bring both the toxic blowpipe with dragon darts and a venator bow with dragon arrows. At the start of the fight, the player can get 4-6 hits with a blowpipe before needing to swap to the venator bow. Make sure that Dusk is next to Dawn while hitting the latter so that the bow will bounce twice on her.
For Dusk, a scythe of Vitur is highly recommended due to Dusk's near non-existent Defence, allowing it to hit very hard and frequently.
During phase 3, the player can get 3-4 hits with a blowpipe before needing to switch to the venator bow. As soon as Dawn reaches 10 or less health, immediately smash her with the rock hammer to save a tick.
During phase 4, the player can save a tick by immediately manually smashing Dusk when his health becomes critical. The player should dump as many special attacks as possible during this time. Allowing for the smashing to occur automatically will cause an extra tick or two to pass before the player actually finishes off Dusk, which can be delayed even longer with gear swaps.
(More on the wiki page of this task.)

From Dusk... is an elite combat achievement which requires the player to kill the Grotesque Guardians 10 times without leaving the instance.
Strategy:
This task can be completed with relative ease by bringing 12-14 super restores, a Saradomin godsword, and Guthan the Infested's equipment to serve as food. While not necessary, an amulet of blood fury can also restore some health while using melee. Flick Piety and Rigour to conserve prayer points.
The Guardians do not deal a lot of damage through prayer, and any unprotected hits can usually be healed back with the Saradomin godsword or Guthan's equipment. They can also drop mushroom potatoes and prayer potions to help prolong trips. Having a lightbearer will double the usage of godsword specials to restore stats.
Without healing equipment you need to minimize damage by avoiding mechanics and off-ticking the Guardians so you can pray against both as described in strategies. Supply drops are helpful but unreliable; you should use Saradomin brews for healing, so bring an extra Super combat potion and Ranging potion to refresh your divine potion boosts, as well as excess Super restores for prayer restoration and in case the bosses drop brews.

... 'til Dawn is a master combat achievement which requires the player to kill the Grotesque Guardians 20 times in a single trip.
Strategy:
Use the following inventory for this task:
Players can swap dragon claws for a saradomin godsword, and the ultor ring for a lightbearer, although these are not necessary unless the player's prayer level is on the lower end. Flick Piety on every attack and turn protection prayers off during various interludes (such as Dusk's charge attack, lightning phase, final phase transition, etc.) to conserve as much prayer points as possible.
Guthan's sustains better than a saradomin godsword in terms of healing, especially if a lightbearer is not being used. The boss also drops mushroom potatoes and one or two 4-dose prayer potions at a time, but don't be too reliant on these for the achievement.
Twenty kills, with an average of 1:30, should take around 30-40 minutes, although kills can fluctuate depending on overall dps and how many times Dawn is allowed to heal on the third phase.

Defence Doesn't Matter II is a master combat achievement which requires the player to kill the Corrupted Hunllef without making any armour within The Corrupted Gauntlet.\nFocus on increasing your dps by crafting a perfected bow and perfected staff, using Rigour and Augury, attacking while moving, and entering the fight with full health and prayer. You can maximize inventory space for food by decanting into 4-dose potions.

Egniol Diet II is a grandmaster combat achievement which requires the player to kill the Corrupted Hunllef without making an egniol potion within The Corrupted Gauntlet.
Strategy:
This achievement can be easily completed by not leaving offensive prayers constantly on during the fight. Either flick them or do not use them.
It is not necessary to flick defensive prayers. However, it is required to pray flick the demi-bosses to avoid taking massive and unnecessary damage. Avoid spending run energy unnecessarily during the preparation phase and fight. If you have time remaining before entering the central chamber, wait out this time to replenish any missing run energy. If possible, walk during the first few tornado attacks, as it will be more valuable to have run energy during the later stages of the fight.
As tier 3 armour has the highest prayer bonus, this can be easily done at the same time as Corrupted Warrior, although some care must be taken to conserve stamina for players with lower agility levels.

Corrupted Warrior is a master combat achievement which requires the player to kill the Corrupted Hunllef with a full set of perfected corrupted armour equipped.
Strategy:
The following materials are required for a full set of perfected armour:
- 13 linum tirinum
- 13 phren bark
- 13 corrupted ores
- 650 corrupted shards
An extra 100 shards are needed for two attuned/perfected weapons, 40 shards for two egniol potions, and 40-80 shards for one or two extra teleport crystals. This makes for a total of 830-870 shards needed.
In order to maximise efficiency during the preparation phase, the player can use the following tactics:
- Avoid moving through previously explored rooms.
- Do not make two perfected weapons.
- Do not collect more than 8 fish. With a full set of perfected armour, very little food is needed for the fight.
- Attack creatures while moving or collecting resources.

Wolf Puncher II is a grandmaster combat achievement which requires the player to kill the Corrupted Hunllef without making more than one attuned weapon, within The Corrupted Gauntlet.
Strategy:
Despite the achievement's name, the player is not required to attack the Corrupted Hunllef unarmed. However, if the player is unable to acquire three weapon frames in time, they can make a bow, a staff and punch the Hunllef for the melee hit.
The simplest strategy is to make one perfected and one basic weapon and switch weapons every 6 hits; bring more paddlefish than usual since the fight will take longer.
The achievement can be completed using the 5-1 strategy so that the Corrupted Hunllef never prays against the one perfected weapon the player makes:
- During the preparation phase, collect three weapon frames and one component for a perfected weapon.
- Make one perfected weapon (preferably one the Corrupted Hunllef did not spawn praying against) and two basic weapons. Otherwise, prepare normally.
- During the fight, strike the Hunllef five times with the perfected weapon and once with the basic weapon it is not praying against. Repeat this process until the end of the fight. Example:
- The Hunllef spawns praying Protect from Magic; the player makes a perfected halberd, a basic bow and a basic staff.
(More on the wiki page of this task.)
Gauntlet Veteran is an elite combat achievement which requires the player to complete The Gauntlet 5 times. Completions of the Corrupted Gauntlet will also count towards this task.
Gauntlet Master is a master combat achievement which requires the player to complete The Gauntlet 20 times. Completions of the Corrupted Gauntlet will also count towards this task.

Perfect Crystalline Hunllef is a master combat achievement which requires the player to kill the Crystalline Hunllef without taking damage from: Tornadoes, Damaging Floor or the Hunllef's Stomp Attacks. Also, do not take damage off prayer and do not attack the Crystalline Hunllef with the wrong weapon, within The Gauntlet.

Egniol Diet is an elite combat achievement which requires the player to kill the Crystalline Hunllef without making an egniol potion, within The Gauntlet.
Strategy:
This combat achievement may be more easily done when attempted alongside the Crystalline Warrior task, due to the Prayer bonus from the tier 3 perfected crystal equipment making prayer flicks less important to perfect while taking less damage.
On the other hand, the resources for tier 3 armour take a long time to gather and may even exhaust your run energy, which cannot be restored with an egniol potion if attempting this task. For players confident in their prayer flicking, it is recommended to use tier 1 armour for this achievement.
For reference, a player with 70 Prayer and tier 1 armour can keep an overhead protection prayer active for 4 minutes and 12 seconds.

Crystalline Warrior is an elite combat achievement which requires the player to kill the Crystalline Hunllef with a full set of perfected crystal armour equipped.
Strategy:
The following materials are required for a full set of perfected armour:
- 13 linum tirinum
- 13 phren bark
- 13 crystal ores
- 650 crystal shards
An extra 100 shards are needed for two attuned/perfected weapons, 40 shards for two egniol potions, and 40-80 shards for one or two extra teleport crystals. This makes for a total of 830-870 shards needed.
In order to maximise efficiency during the preparation phase, the player can use the following tactics:
- Avoid moving through previously explored rooms.
- Do not make two perfected weapons.
- Do not collect more than 8 fish. With a full set of perfected armour, very little food is needed for the fight.
- Attack creatures while moving or collecting resources.

Glough Speed-Trialist is an elite combat achievement which requires the player to kill Glough in less than 2 minutes and 30 seconds. The fight can be attempted at the burning brazier in Zooknock's house.
Strategy:
Before starting the fight, cast vengeance and spellbook swap to the Arceuus spellbook. When the fight starts, summon a thrall and cast vengeance again. If you are using defence lowering special attack weapons, dump your special attacks at the start of the fight, if not, reserve some special attack energy for the third phase. It is not too difficult to quickly chip through the first two phases with regular attacks, vengeance spells and a thrall. You can disable your prayer after casting vengeance to maximize the recoil damage. Between phases you can heal up as you have to run to the next room. In the last phase, use all your special attack energy and cast vengeance when possible. If you are struggling with melee, consider using a bow of Faerdhinen with crystal armour, or if available, a twisted bow.
Dying in the instance will place the player with all items intact back in Zooknock's house. Special attack energy does not regenerate if you die, so consider bringing a lightbearer ring to recharge special attack energy between attempts more quickly.
Equipment:
Inventory
- Special weapon of choice
- 1 Divine super combat potion, Super combat potion or Super set
- 3-4 Prayer potions
(More on the wiki page of this task.)
A Greater Foe is an easy combat achievement which requires the player to kill a greater demon.\nKilling a greater demon in the Wilderness Slayer Cave does not count for this achievement.

Not So Great After All is an easy combat achievement which requires the player to finish off a greater demon with a demonbane weapon.\nStrategy:\nAny monster that is classified as a greater demon for Slayer tasks may be killed to complete this achievement. This includes K'ril Tsutsaroth, and his bodyguard Tstanon Karlak, in the God Wars Dungeon, and Skotizo, in the Catacombs of Kourend.

A Demon's Best Friend is an easy combat achievement which requires the player to kill a hellhound. Killing Cerberus counts for this achievement.\nKilling the skeletal hellhound during In Search of the Myreque does not count for this achievement.\nKilling Bouncer during the Fight Arena does not count for this achievement.

Hesporisn't is a hard combat achievement which requires the player to finish off the Hespori with a special attack.\nFor special attacks that hit multiple times, the last hit needs to be the one that kills Hespori for achievement to be completed. This includes the Arkan blade's special attack, as it immediately hits with a burn along side the regular hit. Additionally, the special attacks of Ancient Warriors' equipment weapons such as Morrigan's throwing axe do not work for the achievement.\nEnchanted bolt special effects can trigger this achievement if the bolt effect activates on the last hit, such as Diamond bolts (e). Emerald bolts (e) have the highest chance of activation, making them also effective for this.

Weed Whacker is a hard combat achievement which requires the player to kill all of the Hespori's flowers within 5 seconds.
Strategy:
Players should use throwing knives to complete the achievement, as they have a fast attack speed. Darts can also be used, but have slightly less range. Flowers have a 100% chance of being hit and dying, so the type of knives or darts being used do not matter. Make sure to have the knives/darts set to rapid. When the fight is beginning, spam-click the first flower. As soon as the experience drop appears, move on to the next flower.
Players with access to Blisterwood stakes set to rapid can hit all the flowers without needing to move.
Alternatively, a combination of a 4-tick powered staff with a built-in magic spell (e.g., Trident of the Swamp) and fast melee weapon can be used. Stand next to one flower and attack the other three flowers using the staff in quick succession, then switch to melee for the fourth flower.
If the flowers are not killed in time, exit the room using the entrance or an emergency teleport, and then return. This will allow for another attempt, instead of killing Hespori and having to grow another one.

Plant-Based Diet is an elite combat achievement which requires the player to kill the Hespori without losing any prayer points.
Strategy:
Players with decent combat stats should be able to kill the Hespori without using Prayer at all. Extra food may be helpful to make up for this.
Prayer drain from Thralls does NOT count, meaning they can be used to aid in the fight.

Hespori Speed-Trialist is an elite combat achievement which requires the player to kill the Hespori in exactly 48 seconds or less.\nStrategy:\nFor strategies on this achievement, see Hespori Speed-Chaser.

Hespori Speed-Chaser is a master combat achievement which requires the player to kill the Hespori in under 36 seconds.
Strategies:
- Waiting for a new Hespori seed to grow with every attempt is not required; if the attempt begins poorly, simply leave the cave, via the exit or teleporting, to redo the fight from the beginning.
- Using a crystal halberd special attack when Hespori is just over 200 health can bring Hespori under 100 health, skipping an entire plant phase.
- Killing Hespori's flowers can be sped up following the strategy section of Weed Whacker achievement.
- You must wait 1 tick before attacking boss after the last flower's xp drop, else the attack will be nulled and do no damage.
- With the rite of vile transference unlocked, you can use the upgraded Death Charge on the second set of flowers, along with a dose of surge potion at 81 Herblore, for a total of 155 special attack energy. This allows, for example, a total of three burning claw special attacks and one crystal halberd special attack all in one kill.
- Kill Flowers. Summon a mage thrall and burning claw spec twice. If Hespori phases, drink surge potion and kill flowers; if not, reset.
- Burning claw spec twice, attack with a strong weapon once if not phased yet. If Hespori phases, cast death charge; if not, reset.
- Crystal halberd spec. If it does not kill, reset.
(More on the wiki page of this task.)

Sleeping Giant is an easy combat achievement which requires the player to kill Obor whilst he is immobilized. This achievement can be completed without opening Obor's chest at the end, allowing players to repeatedly attempt the achievement without needing to spend another giant key to fight Obor.
Strategy:
To complete this task freeze Obor such as by using Bind, Snare, or Entangle before dealing the last hit of damage. Having a high Magic level will make this task increasingly easy, as spells such as Ice Burst, Ice Blitz and Ice Barrage will immobilize Obor for several seconds, allowing the final hit to be dealt more easily.
The Zamorak godsword's special attack cannot be used to complete this task.

Back to the Wall is a medium combat achievement which requires the player to kill Obor without being pushed back more than one square by his knockback attack. This achievement can be completed without opening Obor's chest at the end, allowing players to repeatedly attempt the achievement without needing to spend another giant key to fight Obor.\nStrategy:\nIf using melee, the player should immediately run to the corner of the room, so Obor cannot push them back any further. If using magic, freeze Obor in place using snare or similar to prevent him from using his knockback attack.

Squashing the Giant is a medium combat achievement which requires the player to kill Obor without taking any damage off prayer. This achievement can be completed without opening Obor's chest at the end, allowing players to repeatedly attempt the achievement without needing to spend another giant key to fight Obor.
Strategy:
Using Magic and either Snare or freezing spells is recommended for this achievement. Use the Protect from Missiles Prayer and avoid melee damage at all costs. The achievement will still complete if the player takes damage from the falling rocks while praying Protect from Missiles. Remember to enable Prayers before climbing down to fight Obor. Enabling Prayers during the climb-down may cause the achievement to fail. Make sure to enter the room when Obor is far away from the rocks used to enter the lair, to decrease the chance of Obor hitting before he is caught with a Snare or freezing spell. With a high Magic level, Ice Barrage is recommended.
Players with high melee stats may also choose to try and tank the damage by praying range and equipping good crush armour while trying to end the fight quickly with a high damage spec weapon such as the dragon dagger or dragon claws. While this method is less skill intensive, it does require an amount of luck to pull off and may take several tries.

Fighting as Intended is an easy combat achievement which requires the player to kill Obor on a free to play world. This task does not require you to use a Giant Key to loot the chest.
Strategy:
Bring runes for Earth Blast, and optionally, Snare.
Note that stat boosts from members-only items, such as a super strength potion, will be cancelled by logging into a free to play world.

Alchemical Master is a master combat achievement which requires the player to kill the Alchemical Hydra 150 times.\nStrategy:\nThe minimum amount of Hydras that Konar can assign is 125, so a Bracelet of slaughter is helpful to complete this achievement in a single task.

Unrequired Antipoisons is a master combat achievement which requires the player to kill the Alchemical Hydra without being hit by its acid pool attack.\nStrategy:\nHydra will spit poison blobs in its poison phase and its enrage phase. After the 3rd attack in each phase, the player should prepare to dodge the poison by standing far away or on a location that will not send random poison blobs. After another 9 attacks, be prepared to dodge another poison attack.

Lightning Lure is a master combat achievement which requires the player to kill the Alchemical Hydra without being hit by its lightning attack.\nStrategy:\nThis achievement can be completed by running to avoid the lighting when it spawns, skipping the lightning phase altogether, (similar to The Flame Skipper), or by performing a Lightning skip.

Don't Flame Me is a master combat achievement which requires the player to kill the Alchemical Hydra without being hit by its flame wall attack.\nStrategy:\nThe flame wall attack can be easily dodged by walking away from the flame as it spawns. Otherwise, performing any variation of a 'flame dodge' or The Flame Skipper will be enough to complete the achievement.

Mixing Correctly is a master combat achievement which requires the player to kill the Alchemical Hydra without empowering it.\nStrategy:\nIf the Alchemical Hydra gets sprayed by chemicals from an incorrect vent (relative to its phase), it will become empowered, increasing the damage of its attacks. To complete this challenge, while the Alchemical Hydra is in Green phase (1st phase) it must never be touched by the green or blue vents, the Blue phase (2nd phase) must never be touched by the red or blue vents, and the Red phase (3rd phase) must never be touched by the green or red vents. The Grey phase (4th phase) must never be touched by any of the three vents.

The Flame Skipper is a master Combat Achievement which requires the player to kill the Alchemical Hydra without letting it spawn a flame wall attack.
This achievement will only count as completed if the Hydra does not reach the middle and stop moving before changing phases.
Strategy:
Most players with a twisted bow, dragon hunter lance, or dragon hunter crossbow (with some lucky enchanted bolt effects) will usually complete this achievement at some point during the 150 kill combat task grind, due to high hitting abilities of these weapons. There are a few methods to maximise damage during this phase:
- Vengeance can add up to an additional 52 damage. Cast Vengeance during the Hydra's green or blue phase, so the cooldown timer can expire and be recast immediately after it procs during red phase.
- Lure Hydra onto the blue vent while it is still in blue phase so that it will have its defence reduced as soon as possible after changing to red phase.
- Without access to the above listed weapons, a toxic blowpipe with dragon darts is recommended.
- Use a crystal halberd special or other high hitting weapon for a final hit just before it reaches the centre of the room.
- Optionally, use Spellbook Swap to summon a thrall, which can contribute additional damage, though its impact is negligible.
(More on the wiki page of this task.)

Alcleanical Hydra is a master combat achievement which requires the player to kill the Alchemical Hydra without taking any damage.\nStrategy:\nAll damage from the boss is avoidable; the only issue is the first attack it uses upon entering the boss room, which cannot be predicted. If it attacks with the opposite style that is prayed against, leave the room and try again.

No Pressure is a grandmaster combat achievement which requires the player to kill the Alchemical Hydra using only Dharok's greataxe as a weapon whilst having no more than 10 Hitpoints throughout the entire fight.
Strategy:
Enter the Alchemical Hydra's chamber praying Protect from Magic, as Dharok's armour has higher ranged defence than magic.
If it attacks with ranged:
- Teleport out immediately and try again (requires very quick reactions).
- Tick eat the attack with a low-healing food such as purple sweets or cooked meat, which are also useful if you lose track of which attack is coming next.
- You still have a chance to block the damage with your melee armour stats.
For the rest of the fight, which is the same as a normal melee fight, see Alchemical Hydra/Strategies. Due to the low damage per second afforded by Dharok's equipment, it is likely that the player will face multiple special attacks per phase. This occurs after the ninth regular attack following the first special attack. Make sure to start moving in advance of the second poison blob attacks during the first and fourth phases.
To always avoid the shotgun poison blot after the 3rd/9th attack, run under and through the hydra.
For the lightning attack, start in the north-east corner when the attack goes out, and run west along the northern wall. If the lightning lingers upon reaching the western wall, run south along it.
(More on the wiki page of this task.)

Alchemical Speed-Chaser is a master combat achievement which requires the player to kill the Alchemical Hydra in under 1 minute and 45 seconds.\nStrategy:\nFor strategies on this achievement, see Alchemical Speed-Runner.

Alchemical Speed-Runner is a grandmaster combat achievement which requires the player to kill the Alchemical Hydra in under 1 minute and 20 seconds.
The achievement requires 1100 damage to be dealt in 133 ticks, requiring an average damage of 33 for 4-tick weapons such as Bow of Faerdhinen, and 41.35 for 5-tick weapons such as Twisted bow.
Strategy:
The hydra's massive health pool and high Magic level make the Twisted bow the optimal weapon to complete the task, and Dragon claws are helpful in bursting down a phase. With good gear and enough luck, it is possible to complete with dragon hunter lance or even a toxic blowpipe.
To save time:
- Lure the hydra to each respective chemical pool as soon as possible, blue and red phases should start with hydra already standing on the respective pools to be de-buffed.
- The blue phase should be ended as fast as possible, as getting hit by one of the lightning strikes will bind and damage the player for ~25.
- Clearing the fire phase early avoids unnecessary damage to the player and lost time from the knockback.
- Avoid attack delays by using Guthix rests throughout the fight.
- 80 seconds allows for 4 optimal Vengeance hits, and requires high health at the start of enrage phase:
- Vengeance before entering, there's a 50% chance the first attack will be prayed correctly. If prayed correctly, hold until green phase acid pool removes damage reduction.
(More on the wiki page of this task.)

Working Overtime is a master combat achievement which requires the player to kill the Alchemical Hydra 15 times without leaving the room.
Strategy:
The boss itself is not particularly damaging, only enduring - the only time the player would need to eat is at the start of the kill or if an attack/mechanic is improperly dealt with. While not necessary, a twisted bow is helpful in securing faster kills, which means less prayer restoration used per kill. A Toxic blowpipe can be used to regain small amounts of health periodically. The boss also drops sharks and super restores, but don't rely on these too often.
If you're having trouble, consider taking Armadyl brews as these boost the player's Ranged level (unlike Saradomin brews, which drain it) and give 44 health per inventory slot at 99 Hitpoints.

A Near Miss! is an elite combat achievement which requires the player to complete the Fight Caves after surviving a hit from TzTok-Jad without praying.\nStrategy:\nThe task requires TzTok-Jad to deal at least 1 damage to the player to be completed. As its max hit is 97, players are highly recommended to use consumables to boost above their base Hitpoints, such as anglerfish and Saradomin brews. At minimum, players looking to complete this achievement should have level 84 Hitpoints whilst drinking a Saradomin brew, which boosts the player's health to 98.

Denying the Healers is a master combat achievement which requires the player to complete the TzHaar Fight Cave without letting any of the Yt-MejKot heal themselves or any other monster.\nStrategy:\nYt-MejKot can only heal if they are within melee distance of the player, so players are recommended to use safespots or position them behind other monsters so they cannot reach the player while killing them.

Denying the Healers II is a grandmaster combat achievement which requires the player to complete the Tzhaar Fight Caves without TzTok-Jad being healed by a Yt-HurKot.
Switching worlds during any wave will render this achievement impossible to complete.
Strategy:
In general, this achievement is made easier by luring Jad towards the entrance in the north-east corner of the arena. The healers are spawned in areas away from the cave's entrance, so luring Jad here can give more time to either deal with Jad, or to tag the healers. The most common approach is to use a long-range weapon to attack the healers before they reach Jad. Possible 4-tick weapons with a 10-tile attack range are the Bow of Faerdhinen, crystal bow, or Magic comp bow, set to rapid. Another, riskier but faster approach is to reduce Jad to just above 150 hitpoints, the point at which healers will spawn, then cast Vengeance and use two dragon claws special attacks in quick succession while allowing Jad to hit the player, which is likely to quickly finish it off before any Yt-HurKots have the chance to heal.
Do not attempt this combat achievement on Rotation 5 (the "speedrun" rotation) without dragging Jad away from his spawn, as a healer spawns directly adjacent to its spawn. It is advisable to attempt this on Rotation 7, 8 or 11 as Jad spawns in the middle of the cave.
(More on the wiki page of this task.)

You Didn't Say Anything About a Bat is a master combat achievement which requires the player to complete the TzHaar Fight Caves without being attacked by a Tz-Kih.
Strategy:
Tz-Kihs will appear in 32 out of the 63 waves of the Fight Caves. Tz-Kihs are melee enemies and have near nonexistent stats, so the player should take them out with reasonable ranged weapon, such as a toxic blowpipe or Craw's bow. The latter is recommended in the event that the blowpipe misses or fails to hit, so the player can maintain distance from the Tz-Kih until it is dead.
Logging out or hopping worlds between waves may cause the achievement not to be awarded.

Facing Jad Head-on is an elite combat achievement which requires the player to complete the Fight Caves with only melee weapons equipped. Players are allowed to log out and back into the same world and still be eligible for the combat achievement, but hopping worlds is not allowed.
Strategy:
Equipping a Ranged weapon, Magic weapon, or salamander will cause the task to fail regardless of whether or not they attack anything with it. This includes weapons that primarily have melee bonuses, but can also autocast spells, like the Lunar staff and blisterwood flail. However, manually casting spells with a melee weapon equipped will not fail the task. This means that casting Vengeance, casting blood spells, or summoning thralls with resurrection spells will not fail the task, as long as a melee weapon is equipped.
Using a halberd (preferably a noxious halberd) can make the challenge easier as it allows players to attack from two tiles away instead of one, preventing rangers and magers from attacking with melee.

No Time for a Drink is a grandmaster combat achievement which requires the player to complete the Fight Caves without losing any prayer points.
Strategy:
It is a common myth that 1-tick prayer flicking is required for this task. Lazy flicking the magers and Jad is enough to clear this task, with some room for mistakes.
Players must avoid all Tz-Kihs; getting hit by one will fail the task whether or not it drains a prayer point, automatically disqualifying the player from the achievement. The player will need to safespot as many monsters as possible, especially the Ket-Zeks as these can deal massive damage if their attacks are not protected against. Prayer flicking is still allowed to complete the task. High prayer bonus gear offers a buffer before a prayer point drain, if prayer is left on beyond the first tick.
Thralls can be summoned without failing the task.
The player can be resurrected via the Karamja Elite Diary reward and still be eligible for the task.
The Falador shield 4 resets the player's internal prayer drain counter, which will clear mistakes from leaving prayer on beyond the first tick. The shield cannot be used with full prayer points, but this restriction can be circumvented with thrall spells. Lower tier Falador shields do not work.
The task won't complete if the player hops worlds during the attempt.
(More on the wiki page of this task.)
