Tekton is weakest to crush attacks so using an elder maul, or inquisitor mace is recommended, with a zamorakian hasta/dragon hunter lance as last-ditch alternatives. Inquisitor's armour helps complement the crush-based style with accuracy and damage bonuses, which should help deal plenty of damage to Tekton if he has been successfully debuffed.
For solo-run attempts, be sure raid scaling is set to "0" for the easiest fight, as scaling a raid to "1" doubles boss health.

Dancing with Statues is an elite combat achievement which requires the player to receive kill credit for one of the stone guardians without taking damage from their falling rocks attack.\nUse a flinch method to reduce the chances of the guardians attacking. The falling rock attack has a 3x3 AoE centered on the tile it would fall on, so run two spaces away to avoid getting hit.\nWhile regular accounts only need to do more than 50% of the damage to receive kill credit, Ironmen accounts need to do 100% of the damage for the achievement to count.
Undying Raider is a master combat achievement which requires the player to complete a Chambers of Xeric solo raid without dying.\nThis task will also complete Undying Raid Team.

Shayzien Specialist is an elite combat achievement which requires the player to receive kill-credit for a lizardman shaman without taking any damage from them. Poison damage does not fail the task.
Strategy:
Only one shaman needs to be killed to complete the achievement.
The simplest strategy is to use Ranged with Protect from Missiles, staying out of melee range while running around to avoid their attacks. Players should run from their previous position whenever a shaman jumps (move at least 2 tiles), shoots a green poison blob (move at least 3-4 tiles), and whenever the shamans' purple spawns get near. Bring a superantipoison and a stamina potion. This can be made easier in a solo by waiting until one of the two shamans is on the farthest side of the room as it may not aggro onto the player for a while, allowing the other one to be killed on its own.
Alternatively, safespots can be used to kill the shamans without them being able to retaliate back. However, they will often need to be engaged first and one of the three potential layouts has very poor safespotting that will likely result in both shamans aggro'ing a player in the process. Manipulate the shamans into performing their jump attack (3x3 AoE centred on the target at the time of the mechanic) at the designated area; once the shaman has been lured, use a weapon with a range of 10 to kill them off.
(More on the wiki page of this task.)

Playing with Lasers is a master combat achievement which requires the player to clear the Crystal Crabs without wasting a single orb after activating the first crystal.\nThis task is best completed in a group as solo encounters require the player to bind the crabs in place repeatedly with a hammer and the layout of the room may be unfeasible for completing it.

Cryo No More is an elite combat achievement which requires the player to receive kill-credit for the Ice Demon without taking any damage.\n- Iron players must kill the Ice Demon solo to be eligible.\n- For solo-run attempts, be sure raid scaling is set to "0" for the easiest fight, as scaling a raid to "1" doubles boss health.

Perfect Olm (Solo) is a master combat achievement which requires the player to kill the Great Olm without taking damage from his crystal burst, teleport, fire wall, healing pool, crystal bomb and prayer orb attacks. The player must also not let his hands regenerate during phase 3 and not take consecutive damage from the same acid pool.
Strategy:
Olm starts off each phase beginning with two auto-attacks before performing its first special attack, Crystal Burst. The most dangerous threat for this achievement are the fire walls and teleport portals; if the player is on the Arceuus spellbook, they won't have any ideal means of dispelling the fire walls apart from carrying a water source (e.g watering cans) on them. Teleport portals can also have a range of 10 tiles from the player, which when focused on Olm may make them hard to spot in time.
In order to successfully pull off the achievement, the player must utilise the safespots as shown by the picture to the right. These spots will always force the head to turn accordingly based on its location:
- Spots 1 and 8 always force the head to turn right.
- Spots 4 and 5 always force the head to turn left.
- When running from spot 4, running to spot 2 will ensure the head turns right as long as the right hand has been damaged. If the right hand is not damaged, it will turn to the middle.
(More on the wiki page of this task.)

Perfect Olm (Trio) is a master combat achievement which requires the team to kill the Great Olm without taking damage from his crystal burst, teleport, fire wall, healing pool, crystal bomb, and prayer orb attacks. The player must also not let his hands regenerate during phase 3 and not take consecutive damage from the same acid pool.
Duo Group Ironmen are not required to do this task, as they would lose prestige status. They also will not gain combat achievement points for completing this.
To do this in a solo raid, set scaling to 2. In a duo, set it to 1.
Strategy:
Solo: Follow the Perfect solo Olm strategy. As the task only requires Olm to be killed this way in a trio raid, one or two players can still handle the task, although extra time is likely to be needed due to the scaled stats.
Since the task doesn't disqualify players who die to Olm's standard attacks, players can suicide supplies if necessary.
Trio: If you want to do it as an actual trio, keep the following in mind:
- Lightning special attack hitting you does not fail the achievement. Still avoid it whenever you can since you might get stuck in a poison pool or flame wall.
- The every-other-tick falling crystal attack that can occur during crystal phase does not fail the achievement if it hits you. Tank the hits in order to ensure you do portal special successfully.
(More on the wiki page of this task.)

Blind Spot is a master combat achievement which requires the player to kill Tekton without taking any damage.
Strategy:
You do not need to receive kill credit for Tekton in order to complete this achievement. So it is easiest to get a partner to tank him and do most of the damage while you land one damaging hit. In order to speed up the kill you can have the partner stand on the opposite side of Tekton and hit him only right after he swings at your partner then walk away like you would at guardians.
Lure Tekton to the centre of the arena, away from any pillars of smoke, as these have erratic hitboxes and can deal 1-3 damage when standing on them, disqualifying them from the achievement. Use one of the flinching or running methods to avoid Tekton's standard attacks. Be careful of the fireballs launched during his repair state as they have a 3x3 AoE; while they should generally hit together, they may occasionally desync and hit on different ticks due to travel distance.
Unlike other cox combat achievements, you need to be in the room at the end of the fight to complete the achievement. Entering through Tekton's fire will fail the achievement, meaning the player must be present the whole fight.
For solo-run attempts, be sure raid scaling is set to "0" for the easiest fight, as scaling a raid to "1" doubles boss health.

Blizzard Dodger is an elite combat achievement which requires the player to receive kill-credit for the Ice Demon without activating the Protect from Range prayer.
Strategy:
For solo-run attempts, be sure raid scaling is set to "0" for the easiest fight, as scaling a raid to "1" doubles boss health.
By having another player use protect from range and dodge the demon's attacks in the centre of the room, additional players can stand on the north/eastern walls and avoid the demon's aggression completely. Using Fire Surge will help secure kill-credit over players using ranged.
Ironmen must be the only player damaging the Ice Demon to complete this combat achievement.

Kill It with Fire is an elite combat achievement which requires the player to finish the ice demon off with a fire spell.\nFor solo-run attempts, be sure raid scaling is set to "0" for the easiest fight, as scaling a raid to "1" doubles boss health.

Chambers of Xeric (Solo) Speed-Chaser is a master combat achievement which requires the player to complete a Chambers of Xeric solo run within 21 minutes.
Strategy:
Look for a raid with extremely easy and simple rooms, if possible, try to align this with the grandmaster variant. There is a 4 minute gap between this and the grandmaster variant, though taking either master or grandmaster variants are acceptable for this achievement.
Ideal layouts for a raid can include:
- Vasa, Vespula, Tekton, Tightrope, Crabs
- Vasa, Vespula, Tekton, Crabs, Guardians
- Vanguards, Tekton, Vespula, Tightrope, Crabs
Vasa is a very fast room when a twisted bow is used alongside a dragon warhammer, assuming that the hammer does land at least once in the fight. Vespula can be easily taken out by using either the twisted bow or a Tumeken's shadow. Tekton can be easily dealt with using Osmumten's fang if no Scythe of Vitur or Inquisitor's mace is available. Tightrope can be skipped if needed and crabs are fairly straightforward to do, assuming the ideal layout. This will result in 4 brews, 2 restores, prayer enhances and overloads, which is more than enough for an experienced player at Olm.
Vanguards are only put on the list as it is possible to clear them fast with good gear.
(More on the wiki page of this task.)

Chambers of Xeric (Solo) Speed-Runner is a grandmaster combat achievement which requires the player to complete a solo Chambers of Xeric run in under 17 minutes.
Strategy:
Pick a raid with very fast to clear rooms while minimising supply usage, as the player is expected to no-prep Olm.
Layouts with fast rooms, at least 1 overload and some supplies are ideal. 3 combats and 2 puzzles is the smallest possible layout, Tightrope and crabs are the fastest puzzle rooms allowing 3 combat rooms for the other supplies. Commonly wanted combat rooms are: Vasa (2 Xeric's aid+ and an Overload+) and Vespula (2 Xeric's aid+, Revitalisation+, Prayer enhance+ and an Overload+). Tekton and Muttadile (Need to freeze both muttadiles) can still be used but are usually slower and are substituted for Shamans since the changes that allows Vasa and Vespula to drop overloads.
A (Vasa, Tekton, Vespula, Tightrope, Crabs) layout will provide the player with four brews, two restores, prayer enhances and overload, which should be more than enough for the player to use at Olm. A (Vasa, Shamans, Vespula, Tightrope, Crabs) is a slightly faster layout but results in 1 less restore. Make sure to make the most of your inventory to fit all the supplies, since it is more important to finish the raid than trying to organise in the chest.
(More on the wiki page of this task.)

Chambers of Xeric (5-Scale) Speed-Chaser is a master combat achievement which requires the player to complete a Chambers of Xeric (5-scale) in under 15:00.\nLike other tasks requiring a specific number of players, this combat achievement is not required for Group Ironmen with a smaller group size.

Chambers of Xeric (5-Scale) Speed-Runner is a grandmaster combat achievement which requires the player to complete a Chambers of Xeric (5-scale) in under 12:30.\nLike other tasks requiring a specific number of players, this combat achievement is not required for Group Ironmen with a smaller group size.

Chambers of Xeric (Trio) Speed-Runner is a grandmaster combat achievement which requires the player to complete a Chambers of Xeric (Trio) in under 14:30.\nAny raid layout with enough overload is doable by no-prepping, minimizing tick loss, staying overloaded, and using offensive prayers. Two overloads can be enough with a maximum of one iron: Everyone sips the first overload. One player, the iron if there is one, should pick up a Twisted(+) from Vanguards or Vasa for Olm head. Everyone sips the second overload. The players without Twisted(+) split the remaining two sips of overload. You can easily make time with layouts that include more overload.

Perfect Zalcano is an elite combat achievement which requires the player to kill Zalcano 5 times in a row without leaving or getting hit by the following: Falling rocks, rock explosions, Zalcano powering up, or standing in a red symbol.
Strategy:
The easiest way to obtain this achievement is in large teams, to minimise the amount of dangerous attacks Zalcano may spawn. When running across the room, the player should be ready to dodge red symbols if Zalcano spawns them, although the task is only failed if the player takes damage, and the red symbols do not damage players for three ticks after spawning.
Taking damage from Zalcano's unavoidable pebbles or from standing under her while she has fallen doesn't fail the task, and the streak is not lost if a player stays in the room but does not receive kill credit. It is not required to meet the threshold for a unique drop (indicated by receiving two crystal shards) for a kill to count towards the streak.

Team Player is an elite combat achievement which requires the player to receive imbued tephra from a golem.
Strategy:
The easiest way to obtain this achievement is to kill Zalcano solo, not using any imbued tephra on Zalcano but instead waiting for the golem to spawn and using your imbued tephra on the golem.
The most reliable way to complete this achievement is to attack golems when standing on a blue circle, in order to maximise damage. If there are no blue circles when the golem spawns, try to attack it as soon as possible, so that it's possible to fire multiple tephra at it. Without the blue circle damage boost, it will likely take several tephra to kill a golem.

The Spurned Hero is an elite combat achievement which requires the player to kill Zalcano as the player who has dealt the most damage to her.\nThe achievement checks for the amount of mining damage dealt to Zalcano after breaking her stone armour, rather than checking whether the player is the MVP for that kill (i.e. the one who receives the infernal ashes upon defeating her).

Yarr No More is a hard combat achievement which requires the player to receive kill-credit for K'ril Tsutsaroth without him using his special attack.
Strategy:
The easiest way to complete the combat achievement is to use the Scorching bow, as its special attack always freezes K'ril in place. With sufficient damage, K'ril can be killed without him being able to attack the player at all, guaranteeing the combat achievement. Alternatively, players can use a kiting method to stay out of melee range.
K'ril only uses his special attack against players using Protect from Melee. Therefore, a good strategy that uses melee only is to instead use Protect from Magic along with strong melee armour; a super combat potion and Emberlight or Arclight are also recommended.

Demonic Showdown is a hard combat achievement which requires the player to finish off K'ril Tsutsaroth whilst all of his bodyguards are dead.\nStrategy:\nA good method to complete this task solo (and the similar tasks for each of the respective God Wars Dungeon bosses) is to use a Toxic blowpipe alongside a Serpentine helm to envenom the bodyguards between kills, which will put the minions at near-death by the time the boss is nearly dead.

The Bane of Demons is an elite combat achievement which requires the player to defeat K'ril Tsutsaroth in a private instance using only demonbane spells.
Strategy:
Recoil damage (i.e. ring of recoil, echo boots, or Vengeance), Undead Grasp, as well as thralls, will disqualify players from completing this achievement. Additionally, ironmen instances do not work; players must use private instances for this achievement.
While demonbane spells are effective against most demons, K'ril's magic defences still makes them fairly inaccurate, mandating players to also cast Mark of Darkness to increase their accuracy and damage further. A purging staff will further double their bonuses, though the staff of the dead or toxic staff of the dead are viable alternatives as they too can autocast demonbane spells, and have a special attack that reduces all melee damage by 50% for one minute. Lastly, a slayer helmet (i) may be worn while on a greater demon slayer task to further increase accuracy. Players can also cast Ward of Arceuus to reduce damage taken by 10%.
Inventory:
Most normal supplies can be forgone as this strategy is only to stay for the one kill needed for the combat achievement.
- A cheap form of antipoison, such as an araxyte venom sac
- 2-3 super restores or Sanfew serums if not bringing another form of antipoison
- Runes to cast Dark Demonbane, Mark of Darkness, and Ward of Arceuus
(More on the wiki page of this task.)

Demonic Defence is an elite combat achievement which requires the player to kill K'ril Tsutsaroth in a private instance without taking any of his melee hits.
Strategy:
This can be achieved with the use of Protect from Melee and a bit of luck. K'ril Tsutsaroth has a 1/9 chance to use his 'prayer smash' special attack when praying against his melee attacks, which cannot be avoided and will fail the challenge. Maximising your damage output with the use of weapons such as Arclight and special attack weapons such as dragon claws is recommended to minimise the chance he can perform the attack before dying.
Ironman instances do not work, meaning that ironmen have to use the private instance to complete this task.
Another strategy is to walk under K'ril Tsutsaroth until his health bar disappears, and attacking him once before walking back under him again. If you can succesfully stand under him after every attack, he will never be able to hit you. Switching your NPC attack options to 'always right-click' will make this easier to do. Slower weapons with higher strength bonuses such as the elder maul, godswords and the crystal halberd can be very useful as their low attack speed does not matter when using this method, while they can hit very high on each attack.
(More on the wiki page of this task.)

Demon Whisperer is a grandmaster combat achievement which requires the player to kill K'ril Tsutsaroth in a private instance without ever being hit by his bodyguards.
Strategy:
A simple method to achieve this is to use the 5:0 method with a powerful weapon such as Tumeken's shadow, while replacing some damage-boosting gear (e.g., ancestral robe top, tormented bracelet, magus ring) with tank gear (e.g., blessed d'hide body/justiciar chestguard, barrows gloves, ring of suffering (ri)) for the ranged or mage minion not being prayed against. The damage output should still be high enough to kill K'ril in a few cycles, while offering enough defence to block most of the minions' attacks. An additional benefit of this strategy is that it can be used in a regular extended trip, saving the costs of repeatedly creating private instances for each attempt.
It is also possible to complete this challenge by prayer flicking the minions perfectly. To offset the attacks, start under either the mage minion or ranged minion, so it will attack one tick later than the other, and by kiting the melee minion while flicking the ranged and mage minion; alternatively, the player may start a fresh kill towards the east side of the arena, resulting in the ranged minion moving into attack range later.
(More on the wiki page of this task.)

Demonbane Weaponry II is a hard combat achievement which requires the player to finish off K'ril Tsutsaroth with a demonbane weapon.\nStrategy:\nKilling him with demonbane spells will count towards completion, even without a Purging staff. Kril's health can be lowered with another weapon, but the final blow must be done with a demonbane weapon. Darklight, or its upgraded form, Arclight, are the most readily available for most players.

Ash Collector is a grandmaster combat achievement which requires the player to kill K'ril Tsutsaroth 20 times in a private instance without leaving the room.
Strategy:
As K'ril and his bodyguards drop ashes and not bones, the player's healing will primarily come from using Blood Barrage on stacked Tstanon Karlak and Zakl'n Gritch after each kill. The bodyguards can supplement (though not replace) healing with Sharks or Tuna Potatoes drops.
Due to K'ril's high and unpredictable damage, learning a kiting method (such as the 5:0 twisted bow/tumeken's shadow or the 8/9:0 Bow of Faerdhinen/scorching bow methods) is strongly recommended for this achievement. The scorching bow has the added benefit of binding K'ril with its special attack, with enough DPS to kill him within two specials, which allows for some much easier kills. A Lightbearer and Death Charge can regenerate further special attack for these easier kills (though Death Charge use conflicts with Blood spells, and should only be brought if the player is comfortable flicking the minions instead).
The shared instance for ironmen does not count for this achievement.
Half-Way There is an elite combat achievement which requires the player to kill a Jal-Zek within the Inferno. Jal-Zek is first encountered on wave 35 of the Inferno.

The Floor Is Lava is a grandmaster combat achievement which requires the player to kill TzKal-Zuk without letting Jal-ImKot dig during any wave in the Inferno.
Strategy:
A Jal-ImKot will burrow towards the player if they have not been able to attack them for 50 ticks after the start of a wave. Letting it attack you at any point instantly resets its dig-timer, and allows you more options than a DPS race to kill the enemy immediately after the start of the wave.
A simple approach for this task is to complete it alongside the Budget Setup grandmaster task, utilising a longer ranged weapon, such as the bow of Faerdhinen and full crystal armour, or Eye of Ayak or Tumeken's shadow with mage armour, as it is typically failed when Jal-ImKots spawn further south and cannot easily be reached with the toxic blowpipe.
Otherwise, it is important to be comfortable quickly off ticking common stacks to run within range of the Jal-ImKot soon after the start of the wave to blowpipe it down before it can dig, or letting it attack you so you gain additional time before it digs.

Playing with Jads is a grandmaster combat achievement which requires the player to complete wave 68 of the Inferno within 30 seconds of the first JalTok-Jad dying.\nStrategy:\nSince healers spawn when a Jad reaches half health, it is recommended to trigger the spawn of healers for each Jad before killing the first one. Kill or trap each set of healers as they spawn. After all three Jads have spawned healers and their healers have been dealt with, lower each Jad's health carefully, ensuring not to kill any prematurely. Once each Jad is sufficiently weakened, swiftly kill each Jad in succession.

No Luck Required is a grandmaster combat achievement which requires the player to kill TzKal-Zuk without being hit by him and not taking any damage from a JalTok-Jad.
Strategy:
Jads will appear on waves 67-69. One Jad will appear on wave 67 and should prove to be no problem.
Three Jads will appear on wave 68 with an attack speed of 9 instead of 8 and attack in a staggered rotation to allow players to pray against all three.
While fighting Zuk, players must be behind the Ancestral Glyph before he attacks, as it will block the incoming attack meant for the player. Therefore, if his attack goes for the player instead, the achievement is voided. In addition, a final Jad will appear during the fight when Zuk reaches 480 health for the first time.

Nibblers, Begone! is a master combat achievement which requires the player to kill TzKal-Zuk while not letting any of the three pillars that are provided at the start of the fight be destroyed by the Jal-Nibs.

Wasn't Even Close is a grandmaster combat achievement which requires the player to kill TzKal-Zuk without falling below 50 hitpoints at any point during the Inferno run.
Strategy:
All waves will need to be dealt with cautiously, as all of the Inferno monsters hit very hard and the later waves will consist of multiple monsters that use different combat styles, which can easily combo the player out if their attacks aren't protected against. The primary threats for this achievement generally involve double Jal-Aks, a Jal-Zek with a Jal-Xil, or any combination of the three monsters. Try to heal to full (and overheal if necessary) before the start of the next wave to minimise the chance of falling below 50 hitpoints.
Once the first Jal-Zek appears, players are highly encouraged to have Protect from Magic on before the start of the next wave, as the mager has a max hit of 70, which will drop the player below the threshold if they aren't fully boosted (120 or 121 hitpoints). The other monsters have lower max hits, with the ranger having a max hit of 46. Jal-ImKots have a max hit of 49, but they can only attack in melee distance. In these waves with magers, players can position the monsters and use justiciar armour and Protect from Magic to maximise ranged defence.
During Zuk's wave, the damage is more predictably avoided.
(More on the wiki page of this task.)

Budget Setup is a grandmaster combat achievement which requires the player to kill TzKal-Zuk without using a twisted bow for the entire Inferno run.\nStrategy:\nEffective alternative ranged weapons to the twisted bow include the bow of Faerdhinen or Zaryte crossbow along with a toxic blowpipe. Using a Tumeken's shadow (optionally with an Eye of Ayak) is also viable, although care must be taken due to the lower defences of magic armour.

Nibbler Chaser is a grandmaster combat achievement which requires the player to kill TzKal-Zuk without casting any spells in the Inferno.
Strategy:
Blood Barrage can no longer be used as a means to restore health, so alternate means of healing include the Saradomin godsword (also restores prayer), ancient godsword (less efficient) or toxic blowpipe.
Chinchompas or a venator bow will be needed to kill the Jal-Nibs.
While the achievement's description states that all spells cannot be used, there are some exceptions. For example, summoning thralls and Death Charge will not cause the achievement to be failed. Similarly, the eldritch Nightmare staff special attack does not fail the task despite it being a targeted attack and calculating damage based on magic level and magic strength.

Facing Jad Head-on II is a grandmaster combat achievement which requires the player to kill TzKal-Zuk without using any ranged and magic weapons before fighting him.
Strategy:
Justiciar armour and Dinh's bulwark are recommended for the massive ranged defence bonus and passive damage reduction effect, reducing a good chunk of damage from the ranged mobs during the run. A Saradomin godsword is recommended to restore health and prayer points. Even then, try to get as few enemies as possible attacking to avoid the chances of getting combo'd out, since all of the monsters can hit very hard.
The player is still allowed to cast spells as long as they don't equip a wand or staff; as melee armour provides negative magic bonuses, they will need to be taken off in order for the spells to hit. Alternatively, a Voidwaker and Ancestral robe top likely provides enough positive magic accuracy to allow barrage spells to hit. Note that despite polestaves such as the pharaoh's sceptre and keris partisan being unable to autocast spells, they are still considered magic weapons and will fail the task if equipped.
It is highly recommended to bring both a noxious halberd and scythe of Vitur for this task if the player can manage the monsters.
(More on the wiki page of this task.)

Jad? What Are You Doing Here? is a grandmaster combat achievement which requires the player to kill TzKal-Zuk without killing the JalTok-Jad which spawns during wave 69.\nStrategy:\nJalTok-Jad will appear during Zuk's fight when he reaches 480 or lower hitpoints. As the task requires players to not kill this particular Jad, players will need to watch Jad's animations while moving alongside the Ancestral Glyph to avoid getting killed by Jad. It is beneficial, although not completely required, to know when the Jal-Xil and Jal-Zek will spawn, as to minimise distractions as it is possible for them to attack in sync with each other.

Dress Like You Mean It is a hard combat achievement which requires the player to subdue Tempoross while wearing all four pieces of the angler's outfit. Players may mix and match regular angler's outfit pieces with spirit angler's outfit pieces.\nThe outfit can either be obtained from the Fishing Trawler (15 Fishing minimum) or aerial fishing (43 Fishing and 35 Hunter). However, 34 Fishing is required in order to wear it.

Why Cook? is a hard combat achievement which requires the player to subdue Tempoross, getting rewarded with 10 reward permits from a single Tempoross fight.
Possible Strategies:
Both the solo 5 round strategy and the solo firefighting strategy can be used to get enough points per run. The former is outlined below and will not work with the Crystal Harpoon. Note that Humidify is highly recommended for this strategy:
- Fish 17 and cook all
- Load cannon
- Fish 19 and cook all if possible before 93% Storm Intensity
- Load cannon until you are out of fish
- Damage Tempoross until approximately ~50% Essence
- Fish 19 and cook all if possible before 93% Storm Intensity
- Load cannon until you are out of fish
- Damage Tempoross until approximately ~30% Essence
- Fish 19 and cook all
- Drop all 19 fish on the ground next to one of the nearby cannons
- Fish another 19 and cook all if possible before 93% Storm Intensity
- Load all 19 fish into one of the cannons
- Pick up the 19 fish you dropped earlier and load the other cannon until out of fish
- Finish Tempoross off.
10 reward permits are guaranteed when scoring at least 8,300 points in a single game. Starting from 7,600 points, any further points increase the chance of getting 10 permits.
(More on the wiki page of this task.)

Fire in the Hole! is an easy combat achievement which requires the player to attack Tempoross from both sides by loading both cannons on both ships.
Strategy:
This can be achieved by loading both cannons of one ship, then travelling across Tempoross Cove to load the cannons of the other ship. The four cannons do not need to fire simultaneously.
If attempted during the whirlpool phase, the player will be able to run between ships without the risk of being caught in a wave.

TzHaar-Ket-Rak's Speed-Trialist is an elite combat achievement which requires the player to complete TzHaar-Ket-Rak's first challenge in less than 45 seconds.
Strategy:
An easy way to complete this challenge is to use full Dharok's, a Defence-lowering special attack weapon (elder maul, dragon warhammer, or Bandos godsword), Dinh's bulwark (optional), and Vengeance. Additionally, bring several anglerfish (you will need one for each attempt), super combat potions, and a locator orb. If you don't have a Dinh's bulwark, you can alternatively use chinchompas, darts or throwing knives to get the healers' aggression, which additionally has the benefit of being able to use two Defence-lowering special attacks per attempt, or bringing a DPS spec weapon such as Dragon claws.
Before you enter the challenge, equip the special attack weapon, cast Vengeance, drink a super combat potion, and eat an anglerfish. After you enter the challenge, activate Piety and activate your Defence-lowering special attack. When Jad spawns, instantly attack him. If the special attack does not land and/or Jad hits less than 80 damage, die or exit the challenge and try again. If the special attack lands and Jad hits high, activate Protect from Melee and switch to Dharok's greataxe. Lower your hitpoints to below 10 with the locator orb.
(More on the wiki page of this task.)

Facing Jad Head-on III is an elite combat achievement which requires the player to complete TzHaar-Ket-Rak's second challenge with only melee.
Strategy:
JalTok-Jad's melee attack speed is faster than its Ranged and Magic attacks. Melee attacks will alter the cycles with the other Jad making protection Prayer switches between two Jads much more difficult.
To avoid this, a halberd is highly recommended as it will allow players to maintain the necessary distance to prevent the Jads from attacking in sync with each other. The noxious halberd is the strongest choice due to its higher stats and faster attack speed over the crystal halberd. This is only needed for the first Jad, as the other Jad is less of an issue.
There is no restriction on manually casting magic spells, but a magic weapon cannot be equipped at any point during the fight. Using any dagger which has a +1 magic bonus, will not fail the challenge if used to manually cast spells while equipped; however a Pharaoh's sceptre or Keris partisan will, despite also not having autocast options. This can be useful for barraging the Yt-HurKots to grab their attention, as running out from the centre may result in the Jads attacking in sync.

Facing Jad Head-on IV is a master combat achievement which requires the player to complete TzHaar-Ket-Rak's fourth challenge with only melee.
Strategy:
JalTok-Jad can attack with melee every , as opposed to its normal attack speed when using Ranged or Magic attacks. Melee attacks will alter the cycles with the other Jads making protection prayer switches between four Jads much more difficult.
To avoid this and melee attacks from the first three JalTok-Jads, a halberd can be used to attack with melee from a distance. The last Jad can be killed with any melee weapon while praying protect from melee and switching when necessary. To lure the healers effectively, it is possible to use the special attack of Dinh's bulwark, which can hit all the healers in one attack. Because healers don't spawn on a Jad's east side, prepare for your spec by standing on the west side.
You can use any type of thralls for this Combat Achievement.

Supplies? Who Needs 'em? is a master combat achievement which requires the player to complete TzHaar-Ket-Rak's third challenge without having anything in their inventory.
Strategy:
Using a twisted bow or even a bow of Faerdhinen (with full crystal armour) makes this challenge quite easy. Only attempt with a magic set-up if you own a Tumeken's shadow. Other set-ups will significantly increase kill times. You can pre-pot/eat prior to entering the challenge. It is recommended to use the ancient mace special attack in your POH with max melee gear, eat an anglerfish, and drink a dose of prayer regeneration potion prior to entering. With both 99 Prayer and Hitpoints, this will allow you to enter with 121 HP and up to 142 prayer points depending on gear available, plus an additional 1 prayer point restored every 12 ticks up to a maximum of an additional 66 prayer points. It is advised to also sip a combat style appropriate potion prior to entering.
Only use protection prayers without using any stat boosting prayers such as Rigour. At 99 prayer points, a +15 prayer bonus will allow you 445 seconds (7:24) of prayer during the challenge. At 139 prayer points and +20 prayer bonus, using just protection prayers will last over 11 full minutes allowing you to easily complete the challenge.
(More on the wiki page of this task.)

It Wasn't a Fluke is a grandmaster combat achievement which requires the player to complete TzHaar-Ket-Rak's fifth and sixth challenges back to back without failing. The fifth challenge must be completed before the sixth challenge otherwise it will not be completed.\nAfter completing the fifth challenge, player can safely logout and the progression wont be lost.

Multi-Style Specialist is a master combat achievement which requires the player to complete TzHaar-Ket-Rak's third challenge while using a different attack style for each JalTok-Jad. The healers may be damaged with any combat style without failing the achievement.
Strategy:
Since JalTok-Jads are very resistant to magic, it is advisable to start with ranged. Because Jad's melee attacks are faster than the ranged and magic attacks, killing the second one with magic is advisable, as using melee will likely offset the attack cycles of the two remaining Jads or even synchronize them. Kill the last one with melee, and the challenge is complete.
Recoil damage from a ring of suffering (r) or echo boots along with the sacrifice damage from ancient godsword special attack will cause you to fail this combat achievement.
Thralls can be used, but the style of thrall summoned must match the attack style used to kill each Jad, or you will fail this combat achievement. Therefore, after killing a Jad, it is advised to summon a thrall of the next combat style as you switch your gear.

Stop Right There! is a grandmaster combat achievement which requires the player to defeat The Maiden of Sugadinti in hard mode without letting her blood spawns create more than 15 trails of blood.
Strategy:
Blood spawns can appear at random during the fight against the Maiden, but their chances of appearing significantly increase if the Maiden's splatter attack manages to hit someone; thus, any melee users should carefully watch the Maiden's animations, as they will have less time to react compared to those attacking from afar. As the Maiden is generally killed with melee (as it is significantly higher damage when her Defence level is drained), players should be careful.
If a blood spawn appears, the mager is responsible for freezing it in place; as they have near non-existent stats, there should be no issue of splashing in mage gear. An Ice ancient sceptre can be useful for the task, as it will bind the spawn for 21.6 seconds when using Ice Barrage compared to 19.2 seconds.
An alternate strategy takes advantage of the fact that blood spawns that spawn in the north-east corner of the arena cannot move. To take advantage of this, a player can enter, stand on the north-east corner of the area until a blood splat attack occurs, then intentionally step on it to spawn a blood spawn. Then finish the rest of the kill without stepping on another blood splat.

Personal Space is a grandmaster combat achievement which requires the player to defeat the Pestilent Bloat, in hard mode, with at least three players in the room and without any of them standing on top of each other.
Strategy:
Being able to damage the bloat quickly is essential for this task to avoid spending time trying to avoid standing on top of each other. Try to use the first two set of tiles surrounding the centre piece, with one player following another. In hard mode, chunks of flesh will fall from the ceiling for the entire fight, so players should be mindful of this to avoid taking unnecessary damage and stuns, which can potentially allow the Bloat to damage them. If the bloat manages to attack someone, use Protect from Missiles to reduce damage, since everyone is likely to be hit.
When the bloat is inactive, be mindful to avoid death-dotting on each other, as this will disqualify the team if this occurs.
The team cannot enter after the first stomp(?), as it will fail the task saying "Player A has entered the room late."

Royal Affairs is a grandmaster combat achievement which requires the player to complete the Nylocas room without dying in hard mode without letting a Nylocas Prinkipas change styles.
Strategy:
Nylocas Prinkipas has 300/350/400 health (in <3, 4 and 5-man sizes) and like Nylocas Vasilias, will always spawn in its melee form. It functions much like Vasilias and will change combat styles after 10 ticks (6 seconds), so the team must focus it as soon as it appears in order to complete the achievement.
The required amount of damage per player on average decreases with team size, so attempting this achievement in a 5-man encounter should increase the chances of killing the Prinkipas before they can change combat styles. This should be done with dragon claws or a crystal halberd special as these deal the most amount of damage.
Players on the Arceuus spellbook can use Death Charge (ideally the upgraded variant) to get a lot of special energy without stalling waves. A surge potion is also helpful in restoring special attack.

Harder Mode I is a grandmaster combat achievement which requires the player to defeat Sotetseg in hard mode, without taking any damage from its attacks, sharing the large red ball damage, stepping on the wrong tile in the maze, and dying.
Strategy:
Pray according to Sotetseg's attacks and keep Protect from Melee on until a projectile requires the player to swap prayers. This achievement basically mirrors Perfect Sotetseg in normal mode, with the addition of needing to tick eat the large balls. Players targeted by the large balls must tick eat them as sharing them will disqualify the team from the achievement. It is possible to dodge the damage from these balls if the team manages to phase Sotetseg before they can damage them.
The maze works similarly as in normal mode, but it will be divided among the players sent into the realm; this shouldn't be a problem for anyone however with proper coordination.

Harder Mode II is a grandmaster combat achievement which requires the player to defeat Xarpus in hard mode after letting the exhumed heal him to full and without anyone taking any damage from him.
Strategy:
Harder Mode II is essentially the same as following Perfect Xarpus in normal mode, apart from having much less space to move around in general. As with normal mode, landing dragon warhammer and bandos godsword hits are essential for this task, which is fortunately easier in hard mode as Xarpus' Defence drops to 200 from 250.
Once Xarpus starts the screeching phase, the achievement can be easily completed.

Nylo Sniper is a grandmaster combat achievement which requires the player to defeat Verzik Vitur in a Theatre of Blood: Hard Mode run without letting a nylocas explode during the fight.
Strategy:
Nylocas will spawn in phase 2 and 3 of the fight. Up to three nylocas may spawn, consisting of a mix of Nylocas Hagios, Nylocas Ischyros or Nylocas Toxobolos. The nylocas change styles in hard mode, looping from melee, ranged, and magic every 3 ticks, always in that order. The nylocas will pursue a random player upon spawning, though it is possible for them to focus on one player instead. Use the respective weapon against each nylocas to kill them. Binding the nylocas can make it easier for players to take them down without needing to run a lot.
An effective strategy is to equip an Eye of Ayak and be prepared to attack ranged nylocas as soon as they change. Without any additional magic damage bonus, this will always kill the nylocas in one hit as long as your current Magic level is at least 93.
In phase 2, these are always accompanied by a Nylocas Athanatos. It is recommended to keep the Athanatos alive, as its presence will prevent any additional nylocas from spawning until 35.0% or less health, where two Nylocas Matomenos begin to periodically spawn. The healing that the Athanatos provides can generally be outpaced by the team.
(More on the wiki page of this task.)

Team Work Makes the Dream Work is a grandmaster combat achievement which requires the player to have everyone get through the attack without taking damage when Verzik Vitur, in the Theatre of Blood: Hard Mode, uses her yellow power blast attack while the tornadoes are active. This cannot be completed with one player alive.

Harder Mode III is a grandmaster combat achievement which requires the player to defeat Verzik Vitur in hard mode without using melee weapons during her third phase.
Strategy:
The player has the option to choose between the staff of the dead (as it is considered a magic weapon), a twisted bow or Tumeken's shadow for this achievement.
Verzik has a Defence level of 150 along with +30 slash, +100 magic and +230 ranged defence bonuses. Verzik's magic defence rolls off her Defence level rather than Magic in a manner similar to the ice demon, which can make Tumeken's shadow more consistent and high-hitting. It is best to avoid brewing whenever possible however, as this will reduce its effectiveness.
As long as the player does not die against Verzik, the achievement will be gained.

Pack Like a Yak is a grandmaster combat achievement which requires the player to complete a Theatre of Blood: Hard Mode raid within the challenge time, without anyone dying and without buying anything from the supply chest.
Strategy:
A stamina potion may be helpful to bring for both the Nylocas room and Verzik's fight. Only 1-2 players need to bring one with Boost Potion Share if they share the doses before the Nylocas room and/or before Verzik's web attack.
Players should try to only use supplies at the Nylocas and Verzik's fight. Prayer potions might be needed at the Maiden, Bloat and Sotetseg if necessary, but do not waste too much as the supplies will be needed for Verzik. Plan on saving at least 3 Saradomin brews and 3 Super restores for Verzik's fight in case of mistakes, meaning you should try to bring at least 4 brews and 4 restores into the raid to be safe.
- Avoid extra hits at bloat if they would result in tanking flies or stomps.
- Bring an extra brew and hard food for emergencies and to heal before Nylocas Vasilias or during the waves
- Time Sotetseg's death ball with his shadow maze attack to remove the need to heal off its damage or camp low hitpoints.

Hard Mode? Completed It is a master combat achievement which requires the player to complete the Theatre of Blood: Hard Mode within the challenge time.\nStrategy:\nCompleting the raid in the challenge time is easiest in a group of 4 or 5. Time between the rooms is also counted, so players should avoid spending too much time waiting on teammates and buying supplies.

Theatre: HM (4-Scale) Speed-Runner is a grandmaster combat achievement which requires the player to complete the Theatre of Blood: Hard Mode in a team of 4 players with an overall time of less than 21 minutes.\nLike other tasks requiring a specific number of players, this combat achievement is not required for Group Ironmen with a smaller group size.

Theatre: HM (5-Scale) Speed-Runner is a grandmaster combat achievement which requires the player to complete the Theatre of Blood: Hard Mode in a team of 5 players with an overall time of less than 19 minutes.\nLike other tasks requiring a specific number of players, this combat achievement is not required for Group Ironmen with a smaller group size.

Anticoagulants is an elite combat achievement which requires the player to defeat the Maiden of Sugadinti in the Theatre of Blood: Entry Mode without letting a blood spawn live for more than 10 seconds.
Strategy:
If a blood spawn appears, immediately focus it down. Otherwise, killing the Maiden before she can summon them will also complete the achievement.
You do not need to complete the raid to complete the combat task. As the maiden is always the first boss you fight in a raid, you can complete the task in your best range gear and just resign to exit the raid. Taking only your range gear without any other gear switches means you can have an inventory with maximum food and pots. This allows a fairly easy fight and a quick way to complete the task.

Appropriate Tools is an elite combat achievement which requires the player to defeat the Pestilent Bloat in the Theatre of Blood: Entry Mode with everyone having a salve amulet equipped.\nThis achievement can be completed with any version of the salve amulet.

They Won't Expect This is an elite combat achievement which requires the player to in the Theatre of Blood: Entry Mode, enter the Pestilent Bloat room from the opposite side.
Strategy:
This combat task is as easy as it sounds. You just need to enter the arena on the opposite side from where you enter.
You do not need to finish the raid to complete the combat task. Therefore, if you just leave the raid after entering the arena you can greatly simplify your setup and inventory by just using your best range gear to quickly defeat the maiden, who is always the first boss you will encounter and not bothering to fight the Pestilent Bloat. Useful if you just need 4 combat points to achieve the next combat achievement.
However, it is worth attempting to fight the Pestilent Bloat and try to complete the Appropriate Tools and Chally Time combat tasks by bringing some melee gear and a suitable halberd. (See Theatre of Blood/Strategies for suggest setups you can adapt.)
Completing these 3 fairly easy tasks will reward 12 combat task points and help you on to the next combat achievement reward.

Chally Time is an elite combat achievement which requires the player to defeat the Pestilent Bloat in the Theatre of Blood: Entry Mode by using a dragon halberd or crystal halberd special attack as your final attack.
Strategy:
You do not need to complete the raid to complete the combat task. Therefore, if you just leave the raid after defeating the Pestilent Bloat you can simplify your inventory as the mage gear switch required for later in the raid will not be required. Your inventory can thus hold more food and potions to get you through the task.
It is advisable to take your best range gear to quickly defeat the maiden, who is always the first boss you will encounter, (consider completing the Anticoagulants achievement at this time), then switch to your best melee gear with a suitable halberd to complete this task by killing the Pestilent Bloat with a halberd special attack. (See Theatre of Blood/Strategies for suggest setups you can adapt.)
The They Won't Expect This and Appropriate Tools task can also be easily achieved at the same time as this task. So if you are looking for a few points to get to the next combat achievement unlock, completing these 3 tasks will reward 12 combat task points and help you on to the next combat achievement reward.

Nylocas, On the Rocks is an elite combat achievement which requires the player to freeze any 4 nylocas with a single Ice Barrage spell during a Theatre of Blood: Entry Mode raid. As the achievement is completed immediately after freezing 4 nylocas, the raid does not need to be completed.
Strategy:
The easiest way to complete this achievement is to wait until at least halfway through the Nylocas encounter. When there are enough Nylocas stacked around a pillar, casting Ice barrage on the group will likely complete the achievement.
During Maiden, in groups of 2 or more, there is a chance that the South 4,5 and North 4,5 Matomenos will all spawn. They will clump together after a few seconds and can be frozen in unison, easily completing the achievement.

Just To Be Safe is an elite combat achievement which requires the player to defeat Sotetseg in the Theatre of Blood: Entry Mode after having split the big ball with your entire team. This must be done with a group size of at least 2.\nThe big ball refers to the special attack by Sotetseg where it launches a big red ball that cannot be protected against. When multiple players stand on the same tile, the damage inflicted from the ball is split between the players. This attack is used after Sotetseg launches at least ten magic attacks. *Please note: should you fail to split any of the big ball attacks you must restart the entire raid (you cannot simply die and restart this room). It is advised to turn on Combat Achievement Tasks Failure message.*

Don't Look at Me! is an elite combat achievement which requires the player to kill Xarpus in the Theatre of Blood: Entry Mode without him reflecting any damage to anyone.\nIf you fail this achievement, dying and restarting the fight will not reset it. You must begin a new raid. It may be helpful to use a slower weapon, attacking only once or twice per Xarpus's turn, to not fail. Using a blowpipe may cause accidental attacks.

No-Pillar is an elite combat achievement which requires the player to survive Verzik Vitur's pillar phase in the Theatre of Blood: Entry Mode without losing a single pillar.\nStrategy:\nHave every player use the Dawnbringer's special attack multiple times to quickly end the encounter. Avoid teammates spreading between multiple pillars. If one pillar is taking too much damage, preemptively move to another.

Attack, Step, Wait is an elite combat achievement which requires the player to survive Verzik Vitur's second phase in the Theatre of Blood: Entry Mode without anyone getting bounced by Verzik.\nStrategy:\nIf you fail this achievement you can die and re-attempt Verzik within the same raid. You do not need to fully complete the raid to finish this task; you must simply defeat Verzik's 2nd phase without getting bounced.

Pass It On is an elite combat achievement which requires the player in the Theatre of Blood: Entry Mode, to successfully pass on the green ball to a team mate.
The green ball is a special attack launched by Verzik Vitur in her third phase.
Strategy:
The ball must either target the player or be passed from another teammate in order to attempt to pass it to another player. Once the ball is targeting the player, stand near another player to bounce the ball and complete the achievement. Right-click following another player is an easy way to stay close to them.

Theatre of Blood: SM Speed-Chaser is a master combat achievement which requires the player to complete an Entry Mode Theatre of Blood run within 17 minutes, not including time between rooms. This can be completed with any group size.\nStrategy:\nEntry mode should prove to be no problem for most players; the only issue will be the Nylocas room and it is recommended to run a trio so the room can be cleared without much hassle.

Into the Den of Giants is an easy combat achievement which requires the player to kill a hill giant, moss giant, and a fire giant in the Giants' Den within the Shayzien region.\nLocation:\nThe Giants' Den is in north-west Shayzien on the south-east side of Lake Molch. The closest teleport is fairy ring code . Players can also use the Shayzien teleport in the Kharedst's memoirs/Book of the Dead and run west.

Sit Back and Relax is a medium combat achievement which requires the player to deal 100 damage to creatures using undead thralls. This can be accomplished accumulatively across multiple undead thrall casts and multiple enemies.

Perfect Phosani's Nightmare is a grandmaster combat achievement which requires the player to defeat Phosani's Nightmare while only taking damage from husks, weakened parasites and power blasts while also not getting slowed by spores or letting a sleepwalker reach her.
Strategy:
The task is fairly achievable as the player should always be aiming to achieve a perfect kill anyway, as any mistakes result in harsh damage dealt.
Mechanically, the largest threat is Spores, as each spore has a 3x3 AoE, meaning the player must be careful while navigating across totems.
Because the task also requires no sleepwalkers to reach the boss, Dreamland Express is mandatory.

Phosani's Speedchaser is a master combat achievement which requires the player to defeat Phosani's Nightmare in under 7 minutes and 30 seconds.\nStrategy:\nFor strategies on this achievement, see Phosani's Speedrunner.

Phosani's Speedrunner is a grandmaster combat achievement which requires the player to defeat Phosani's Nightmare in under 6 minutes.
Strategy:
Good gear is required for the achievement. Scythe of Vitur with Inquisitor's armour is recommended, but an Inquisitor's mace or Soulreaper axe with Bandos armour will suffice to make time. For the totems, full magic switch and a Tumeken's shadow or an Eye of Ayak are also recommended. Although very unlikely, it is realistically possible over hundreds of kills with an abyssal bludgeon and trident of the swamp as well, although this requires good execution of mechanics, a great deal of luck, and saving time whenever possible (such as eating in between phases). A Crimson kisten or Voidwaker is helpful for its consistent and high-damage special attacks.
There are some strategies that may be used to save time beyond standard execution and minimising time wasted:
- Using a Scythe of Vitur to deal the finishing blow on the last totem of each phase; this causes it to register as charged one tick sooner due to the overkill hitsplat
- Using a ham joint on husks and elder maul/godsword (on crush) on the parasites to immediately kill them with minimal ticks wasted
- Using a lightbearer to perform additional special attacks in the overall fight, Death Charge on husks, parasites or sleepwalkers and bringing an ultor ring switch
(More on the wiki page of this task.)

Crush Hour is a master combat achievement which requires the player to defeat Phosani's Nightmare while killing every husk and parasite that appears in a single hit.
Strategy:
Both the husk and parasite will take damage equal to the player's maximum hit if a weapon with a crush attack style is used to attack them. Husks have 20 health and can be instantly killed by most forms of crush-based weaponry, while Parasites have 55 health, which can be dealt with using a strong two-handed weapon like a godsword, elder maul, soulreaper axe or the special attack of the dragon mace. The unweakened variant gains extra health, which is too high for these weapons.
Note that if a thrall attacks either at the same time the player does, the achievement will fail.

I Would Simply React is a master combat achievement which requires the player to defeat Phosani's Nightmare without having it disable their prayers.\nStrategy:\nThe prayer disabling mechanic only takes place in phase 3, doing so prior to launching an incoming attack; players need only deactivate their protection prayer right after the attack lands.

Dreamland Express is a master combat achievement which requires the player to kill Phosani's Nightmare without a sleepwalker reaching her during her desperation phase and damaging the player.
Strategy:
The Nightmare in phase 4 will have 150 health. Acceptable special attacks include the crimson kisten, Voidwaker, dragon claws, and granite maul (with an ornate maul handle attached) in that order. The kisten is the most consistent of the four due to taking advantage of the Nightmare's weakness to crush, while the Voidwaker is only slightly worse than it due to the lower damage range despite having a higher max hit and guaranteed accuracy.
The first sleepwalker will spawn as soon as the phase begins, and will reach the Nightmare in ~15 game ticks, damaging the player around ~17-18 ticks. This will allow for four attacks with a 4-tick weapon such as an Inquisitor's mace, or three with a Scythe of Vitur. With high-hitting special attacks, the player should be able to subdue the Nightmare before the first sleepwalker even reaches her.
If the sleepwalker ends up reaching the Nightmare, the player is only disqualified if pink petals fall on the player, as this indicates damage was inflicted. If these petals do not appear as the Nightmare is subdued, the player will not be damaged.

Can't Wake Up is a grandmaster combat achievement which requires the player to defeat Phosani's Nightmare five times in a row without leaving her dream.
Strategy:
With a proper Phosani's Nightmare kill, the player's only source of damage should come from sleepwalkers at the end of phases 1-3, parasites when they burst from the player, and any sleepwalkers that reach Phosani's Nightmare during phase 4.
Since the player's inventory will be full of prayer restoration potions, this will leave them with no food to recover from mistakes. Ideal substitutes to restore health from chip damage and minor mistakes should be done with an amulet of blood fury, Sanguinesti staff, and a Saradomin godsword. The latter requires special attack energy however, and has to be used on a parasite, sleepwalker or husk to get the most out of it.
Phosani's Nightmare can provide some supplies in the form of Saradomin brews, prayer potions, Sanfew serums, bass, and sharks, which will last for 30 minutes in the instance. As the player should generally take minimal or no damage from mechanics, prayer potions and Sanfew serums are much more vital for the achievement. Try to line a kill up with food or potion drops, depending on what is brought more. Food is more common than potions, so it may be best to start with a full inventory of potions rather than food.
(More on the wiki page of this task.)
Nex Master is a master combat achievement which requires the player to kill Nex 25 times.\nStrategy:\nThis achievement can be quickly completed by joining the any of the Nex mass worlds.

A siphon will solve this is a master combat achievement which requires players to kill Nex without letting her heal from her Blood Siphon special attack.\nStrategy:\nPlayers must not attack Nex after she shouts as any damage done during that period will heal her instead. Any Blood Reavers that spawn must also be killed before she uses the special attack again.

Contain this! is a master combat achievement which requires players to kill Nex without having anyone take damage from her Containment and Ice Prison attacks.\nStrategy:\nPlayers must stay away from melee distance upon her using her Containment attack and quickly free any imprisoned teammates upon her using her Ice Prison attack. Both Osmumten's fang and Dragon warhammer are particularly accurate against the ice walls, but any crush weapon will work well.

There is no escape! is a master combat achievement which requires players to kill Nex without having anyone take damage from her Smoke Dash attack.\nStrategy:\nPlayers can avoid this attack by standing on the outside of the arena before the attack. If standing in melee distance, Nex will look at the direction she intends to dash towards prior to the attack as a warning indicator to avoid that lane.

Nex Duo is a grandmaster combat achievement which requires players to kill Nex with only two or less players.\nThe task must be completed while there are two or less players in Nex's prison at the start of the fight.

I should see a doctor is a grandmaster combat achievement which requires players to get kill credit for Nex while a player is infected with Nex's Choke attack.\nStrategy:\nFor the task to be completed, players must purposely spread the virus to other players for the entirety of the fight. Players will cough four times (three with a slayer helmet) for each cough, which resets if they infect another player with it. The best way to complete the achievement is to have two or three players purposely infect each other while the rest of the team takes down Nex. These players should ideally not engage Nex in battle to avoid spreading the virus to other players who will be killing Nex.

Perfect Nex is a grandmaster combat achievement which requires players to kill Nex while qualifying for the completion of the following tasks: There is no escape!, Shadows Move..., A siphon will solve this, and Contain this!.
This means the player must kill Nex without anyone doing the following:
- Taking damage from Nex's Smoke Dash, Shadow Smash, Containment, and Ice Prison attacks
- Attacking Nex whilst she is performing her Blood Siphon attack
Despite being a grandmaster task, it can be attempted with any amount of players. If attempting in a large group, communication is helpful to avoid failing the achievement.

Shadows Move... is a master combat achievement which requires players to kill Nex without anyone being hit by her Shadow Smash attack.\nUpon the shadows appearing beneath the player, they will have three ticks (1.8 seconds) to move out of it before they erupt and damage the player.

Tombs Speed Runner is a master combat achievement which requires the player to complete the Tombs of Amascut raid within 18 mins at any group size, at level 150 or above.
Strategy:
When attempting to complete the combat achievement, the following are the approximate times which the player should aim for each stage of the raid:
Gear Recommendations, for a duo, include max armour for all 3 combat styles: Torva, Masori, and Ancestral. Twisted Bow, Dragon Arrows, Blowpipe, Zaryte Crossbow, Tumeken's Shadow, Avernic Defender, Dragon Dagger, Dragon Claws, and one player with Thralls with the other player on the Lunar Spellbook for Vengeance/Vengeance Other. Both players could also use the Lunar Spellbook and use spellbook swap to use Thralls and Vengeance.

Tombs Speed Runner II is a grandmaster combat achievement which requires the player to complete the Tombs of Amascut raid within 20 minutes, with any group size, at level 300 or above.
This task is usually not done directly, instead, at the same time as Tombs Speed Runner III, as completing that task will satisfy this task. However, with strong enough gear and experience, this task can be easily completed on its own at a 300 raid level.
- Hit 300 raid level while not using any path invocations, do use a 25 minute timer and hardcore.
- Avoid Medic, More Overlords, and Double Trouble, as they significantly slow the raid down.
- Use thralls. Spellbook swapping can be useful but is not necessary in max. Every path boss and Wardens' P2 can be venged.
- Bring a pickaxe and an empty slot to avoid inventory management issues.
- Use liquid adrenaline, death charge, and a surge potion to constantly use burning claws, zaryte crossbow, or voidwaker special attacks.
- Death charge baba baboons if they are in a good spot (they are 1 ticked), pre-death charge kephri (swarms, overlords), and pre-death charge Akkha (shadows).
- P2 Core can be death charged during the first down, it can only be death charged during the final down if you kill it on the last hit.
- Swarm both of Kephri's phases.
- Butterfly Akkha to ensure he stays in melee.
(More on the wiki page of this task.)

Tombs Speed Runner III is a grandmaster combat achievement which requires the player to complete the Tombs of Amascut raid in an 8-man party within 18 minutes, at raid level 300 or above.
Unlike the Theatre of Blood, speed-based achievements for the Tombs of Amascut count the overall time rather than the challenge time.
Like other tasks requiring a specific number of players, this combat achievement is not required for Group Ironmen with a smaller group size.
Strategy:
All players should ideally have a high Mining level to clear Het's challenge in one cycle to avoid wasting extra time with the 1-tick pre-mining method to get an additional hit in. All players are required to have near or best-in-slot gear as players must burst through the bosses very quickly. The bosses will have ~5.78 times the amount of health they would in solo. As it is important to move fast in between rooms it is also recommended to leave some inventory space, as to not have to drop and pick up items. With proper play food won't be needed until Wardens, where one should use Ambrosia.
Selecting easy invocations will minimise frustration during the attempt, and it is important that players do not die during the bosses, as even one player dying can significantly set the team back.
The zaryte crossbow with Ruby dragon bolts (e) can deal a lot of damage with its special attack.
(More on the wiki page of this task.)

You are not prepared is a master combat achievement which requires the player to complete a Tombs of Amascut raid using only supplies provided by the Helpful Spirit without dying, at level 150 or above. The task will fail if any players in the raid use outside supplies.
Strategy:
Players should pre-pot (including with an extended anti-venom+) before entering the raid. Using a Falador shield to restore prayer and the Keris partisan of the sun special attack or Blood Spells to restore health will not fail the task. Health, prayer, run energy and special attack are also restored after clearing each path.
It is recommended to prioritise taking nectar and tears of Elidinis from the Helpful Spirit. Ambrosia is also useful as it is the only way to cure poison or venom. Start with Zebak and Kephri first since they can be cleared with little damage taken, then take care to avoid the Cursed Baboon's venom trails in the Path of Apmeken.

Helpful spirit who? is an elite combat achievement which requires the player to complete a Tombs of Amascut raid at level 150 or above without relying on the Helpful Spirit for supplies. The raid must be completed deathless by the entire party and will fail if any players in the raid use supplies from the Helpful Spirit.
Strategy:
Bring a 4-dose potion of super combat and ranging. For a magic boost, bring an imbued or saturated heart instead. Ancient and forgotten brews can be used in place of the heart, but this will drain melee stats in the process.
As the player will not have access to smelling salts and liquid adrenaline, be prepared to three cycle the Warden on phase 2. Other than that, the bosses can be killed fairly easily on a raid level of 150 with good gear.

Resourceful Raider is a master combat achievement which requires the player to complete the Tombs of Amascut raid while having the "Dehydration" and "On a Diet" invocation on and no players dying, at level 300 or above.
Strategy:
To complete this task, it is highly recommended that the player has an amulet of blood fury and Keris partisan of the sun. A Sanguinesti staff is helpful, but not absolutely required if the player possesses Tumeken's shadow.
On a Diet prevents players from using solids (e.g sharks) and also prevents the Helpful Spirit from giving Silk dressings. Dehydration prevents players from using potions to heal (e.g Saradomin brews), which also means that players cannot use nectar or ambrosia either.
The only bosses where players may take significant damage would be Wardens and Akkha, as Zebak, Kephri and Ba-Ba should not deal any significant damage at all due to their attacks being easily avoidable and/or blocked. The player's main source of healing will be from the sun keris, as its passive restores 12 health and overheals to 20% of their base Hitpoints level at the cost of 5 prayer points. This effect is particularly useful at the Wardens' phase 3 to heal off the skulls during the interludes.
(More on the wiki page of this task.)

But... Damage is a master combat achievement which requires the player to complete a Tombs of Amascut raid without using any tier 75 or higher equipment, at level 300 or above.
Strategy:
As tier 75 or higher equipment cannot be used, players will be unable to use most reasonable weapons and equipment that would make the raid faster. The second-best alternatives to use in lieu of them would be the gear setup below.
If crystal armour is outside of your ability/price, hunters' sunlight crossbow, an odium ward and moonlight antler bolts are good alternatives to the crystal bow as the high attack speed can compensate for some of the accuracy and strength loss. Thralls are allowed. Burning Claws and Belle's Folly are eligible and can be brought in as a spec weapon and stab weapon respectively.
Unlike the tier 65 Keris partisan, the Keris partisan of the sun, Keris partisan of breaching, Keris partisan of amascut and Keris partisan of corruption cannot be brought into the raid as they require 80 Attack.
Below is an example equipment and inventory that can be used to complete this task. Quantities and ratios of supplies needed is very dependant on how experienced a player is with the Tombs of Amascut raid. Example inventory might not apply to everyone, and players should make adjustments based on their own skills.
(More on the wiki page of this task.)

Chompington is a master combat achievement which requires the player to defeat Zebak using only melee attacks without dying, at raid level 150 or above. The achievement will be earned immediately after defeating Zebak so the raid does not need to be completed.
Strategy:
At the minimum raid level of 150, Zebak will have 930 health. Zebak's melee attack hits the hardest and can also apply a bleeding effect that deals additional damage if the player moves. Assuming no path levelling is active (which should most likely be the case), Zebak will have an attack speed of 7, or once every 4.2 seconds. Once he enrages, his attack speed increases to 4, or every 2.4 seconds.
Use the best melee weapons and armour you have access to, prioritising melee accuracy and strength bonuses over defensive bonuses. Defence reducing special attacks, such as the Bandos godsword's, can be used since like Ba-Ba he does not reset his Defence level. However, his Defence can only be lowered to 50 (from 70 and before modifications). He has fairly high defensive bonuses (+160 stab, slash and +260 crush), so Osmumten's fang is highly effective due to its passive effect. All melee damage from Zebak can be avoided by using a flinching method. This is done by attacking Zebak from three tiles away, and immediately after, running out of his melee attack range.
(More on the wiki page of this task.)

Fancy feet is a master combat achievement which requires the player to complete phase three of The Wardens in a group of two or more, using only melee attacks and without dying, at raid level 300 or above. The 'Insanity' invocation must be activated.
Strategy:
Insanity can only be toggled on when both "Overclocked" and "Overclocked 2" are active, which when combined with "Insanity" will make the Warden attack every 3 ticks.
The Warden will have 1940 health per player at a raid level of 300, resulting in it having a total of 1940* party size health. Each slam attack will deal roughly 40-50 damage if not avoided. The player must move immediately after attacking to avoid getting hit by the slam, as there is no time to dodge the attack when within five tiles from the boss. The boss will also have four interlude phases entwined at 20% health intervals which release more Energy Siphons in a different layout compared to solo, however despite having "Insanity" there is still a larger amount of time to reverse the skulls before they explode. It is possible to survive with 80+ health with one skull untouched, but two or more result in instant death unless the player somehow manages to avoid the resulting explosion. Supply invocations should be left untouched, and this should leave players with a significant amount of supplies entering the Wardens.
(More on the wiki page of this task.)

Hardcore Tombs is an elite combat achievement which requires the player to complete the Tombs of Amascut raid solo without dying, at level 150 or above. The Hardcore Run invocation does not need to be active in order to complete the achievement.

Perfect Het is an elite combat achievement which requires the player to complete the Path of Het challenge room without taking any damage from the light beam or orbs, and destroying Het's Seal in one cycle, at raid level 150 or above.
Strategy:
Level 85 Mining (boostable from 82 with a Dragon pickaxe) is required for this task in a solo encounter in order to deal enough damage to Het's Seal in one cycle. There is more leeway in group encounters depending on the Mining level of the other teammates and if they are one-tick clicking the pillar before the beam hits the shielded statue, as this provides an extra hit to the statue before the next cycle starts (see Tombs of Amascut/Strategies for the one-cycle method).
The team should take time setting down mirrors to ensure that the beam won't hit them as they set it and watch out for any orbs that appear while setting the mirrors and mining the pillar, as they have a notorious habit of forcing players to move out of the way when the pillar is being destroyed.
A boosted Mining level of 100 or higher will allow destroying the core without the one-tick prep in a solo encounter.

Perfect Akkha is a master combat achievement which requires the player to complete Akkha in a group of two or more, without anyone taking any damage from the following: Akkha's attacks off-prayer, Akkha's special attacks (orbs, memory, detonate), exploding shadow timers, orbs in the enrage phase or attacking Akkha with the wrong style. The player must have all Akkha invocations activated.
Strategy:
Using a melee thrall in the final phase of the fight will fail this combat achievement. It is not known whether this is intended or a bug. However, as Akkha has a chance to change his combat style with every special, it is not recommended to use thralls when attempting this achievement, even if the player starting the encounter is confident with their "butterfly" technique.
As Double Trouble needs to be activated with multiple players, the player butterflying Akkha should dodge the memory attack in the middle, while other players should use the "staircase" technique to skip the memory attack at the edges of the arena. If Akkha switches styles and uses black orbs at the same time, it may be safer to stay still and flick protection prayers, rather than attempting to flinch.
Since the achievement is under Tombs of Amascut, the fastest method is to attempt the achievement with a raid level of 150 with all Akkha invocations active, reducing his health.

Perfection of Het is a grandmaster combat achievement which requires the player to complete Perfect Het and Perfect Akkha in a single run of the Tombs of Amascut raid at raid level 300 or above.\nStrategy:\nPerfect Het and Perfect Akkha do not need to be completed in succession. As death invocations do not need to be enabled, players that complete Perfect Het and then fail Perfect Akkha can all die and re-attempt Perfect Akkha without having to redo Perfect Het.

Perfect Apmeken is an elite combat achievement which requires the player to complete the Path of Apmeken challenge room in a group of two or more without allowing any dangers to trigger, standing in venom, or being hit by a volatile baboon, while completing the room within three minutes, at raid level 150 or above.
Strategy:
Hammers and Neutralising potion are provided in crates in the room before the challenge can start.
When the first player enters the challenge area, they will obtain Apmeken's Sight, which allows them to identify dangers and resolve them before they damage the team. If the pillars have an issue, call out P; if the vents have an issue, call V. If corruption is spreading, death-dot (in larger groups) or use the potion on the corrupted player (smaller groups).
Freeze any Cursed Baboons and immediately kill them to avoid spreading venom. Volatile Baboons can be easily avoided as their explosion is a 3x3 AoE centered around them; they can also be killed, but it is not required.
Following the 29 May 2024 update to the Path of Apmeken, this achievement is significantly easier as the baboons have very little health and can be easily killed in one or a few hits.

Perfect Ba-Ba is a master combat achievement which requires the player to defeat Ba-Ba in a group of two or more, at raid level 150 or above, without anyone taking any damage from the following: Ba-Ba's Attacks off-prayer, Ba-Ba's slam, rolling boulders, rubble attack or falling rocks. No sarcophagi may be opened. The player must have all Ba-Ba invocations activated.\n- This Combat achievement CAN be re-attempted by wiping.\n- This combat achievement is not failed if a player is struck by bananas.

Perfection of Apmeken is a grandmaster combat achievement which requires the player to complete Perfect Apmeken and Perfect Ba-Ba in a single run of the Tombs of Amascut raid at raid level 300 or above.
Strategy:
The Path of Apmeken does not need to be completed in 3 minutes, as is normally required for Perfect Apmeken. Additionally, it and Perfect Ba-Ba do not need to be completed in succession.
