As death invocations do not need to be enabled, players that complete Perfect Apmeken and then fail Perfect Ba-Ba can all die and re-attempt Perfect Ba-Ba without having to redo Perfect Apmeken.

Perfect Crondis is an elite combat achievement which requires the player to complete the Path of Crondis challenge room without letting a crocodile get to the tree, without anyone losing water from their container and in under one minute, at raid level 150 or above.\nStrategy:\nSince deaths restart this task, one (except hardcore iron men) may save a few ticks by entering the puzzle room just to get the water container, then dying to restart the task, as it will appear in the inventory after death. Also, in case one fails, a Locator orb or Dwarven rock cake may be used to reset the task faster.

Perfect Zebak is a master combat achievement which requires the player to defeat Zebak without taking any damage from incorrectly prayed attacks (excluding his blood magic), poison pools, blood spawns, and waves. All of his invocations must be activated to complete the task at raid level 150 or above.
Strategy:
As Upset Stomach will be active, remember to take note that the water jugs have a 3x3 AoE and acid pools 5x5.
Taking damage from Zebak's roar attack will not cause the achievement to fail, so it can be significantly easier to tank the roar attack each time it happens and focus on dealing damage instead of setting up the jugs. Make sure the tile in front of you and a few tiles behind you are clear to not get pushed into acid during the attack. If one is specifically going for this achievement and healing is a concern for tanking, one can simply disable any of the lives invocations and die repeatedly to Zebak with the help of a Locator orb or Dwarven rock cake to obtain enough Honey locusts, which are stackable and can overheal above max health. Simply leave the raid after successfully completing the achievement.
With sufficient DPS, it's possible to skip one of the four special attacks Zebak would use, minimising the chances of failing the achievement as the acid pools are the only concern for the task.
(More on the wiki page of this task.)

Perfection of Crondis is a grandmaster combat achievement which requires the player to complete Perfect Crondis and Perfect Zebak in a single run of the Tombs of Amascut raid at raid level 300 or above.\nStrategy:\nPerfect Crondis and Perfect Zebak do not need to be completed in succession. As death invocations do not need to be enabled, players that complete Perfect Crondis and then fail Perfect Zebak can all die and re-attempt Perfect Zebak without having to redo Perfect Crondis.

Perfect Scabaras is a master combat achievement which requires the player to complete the Path of Scabaras challenge room in less than a minute without anyone taking any damage from puzzles, at raid level 150 or above.\nStrategy:\nThe achievement is best done in a solo encounter while avoiding the pillars room, since this room is a guessing game and can take a while to solve. The last puzzle is incapable of damaging players. A fast way to reattempt the combat achievement is to log out of the raid and start a new raid.

Perfect Kephri is a master combat achievement which requires the player to defeat Kephri in an group of two or more players without taking any damage from egg explosions, her auto-attacks, exploding scarabs, bodyguards (chip damage from range and melee bodyguards does not disqualify if prayed against, neither does poison damage) and dung attacks, at raid level 150 or above. In addition, players must not let any Agile Scarabs hatch.\nUnlike Perfect Ba-Ba, Perfect Akkha, and Perfect Zebak, this combat achievement does not require any Kephri invocations to be enabled.

Perfection of Scabaras is a grandmaster combat achievement which requires the player to complete Perfect Scabaras and Perfect Kephri in a single Expert mode run of the Tombs of Amascut raid.
Strategy:
Path of Scabaras does not need to be completed in less than 1 min, as is normally required for Perfect Scabaras. Additionally, Perfect Scabaras and Perfect Kephri do not need to be completed in succession.
As death invocations do not need to be enabled, players that complete Perfect Scabaras and then fail Perfect Kephri can all die and re-attempt Perfect Kephri without having to redo Perfect Scabaras.

Perfect Wardens is a master combat achievement which requires the player to defeat the Wardens in a group of at least two players, while not taking damage from any avoidable attacks, while having all of their invocations enabled, at raid level 150 or above.
Strategy:
Phase 1 has two possible attacks that will disqualify the player - standing next to the obelisk when it is destroyed causes an explosion that will fail the task, as well as getting hit by the pyramids that come down.
Phase 2 begins to introduce attacks that will disqualify the player if they are not dealt with. For the purposes of this task, Elidinis' Warden should be fought instead of Tumeken's Warden as it will not try to chase after players, so they can focus solely on using Protect from Missiles or Protect from Magic. Tumeken's phantoms are also significantly easier to handle. Red skulls indicate a magic attack, while plain skulls indicate a ranged attack. The Warden will also launch prayer-disabling projectiles in the form of a scimitar, arrow or orb, in which Protect from Melee/Ranged/Magic should be used to block the attack. Failing to pray against the attacks will disqualify the players from the achievement.
The obelisk will also cycle between three special attacks for the duration of phase 2, Windmill, Lightning and Converging Beam.
(More on the wiki page of this task.)

Insanity is a grandmaster combat achievement which requires the player to complete Perfect Wardens in the Tombs of Amascut raid at level 300 or above.\nStrategy:\nAs death invocations do not need to be enabled, players can all die and re-attempt Wardens without having to redo the entire raid.

Amascut's Remnant is a grandmaster combat achievement which requires the player to complete the Tombs of Amascut raid at level 500 or above without anyone dying.
Strategy:
A raid level of 500 will increase the enemies' stats by 200% and health by 150%, making each boss somewhat challenging in itself.
Learning how to use various advanced tactics will help significantly in the raid, as conserving supplies for the Wardens is essential to successfully complete the task.
Equipment and Inventory:
A Tumeken's shadow is the most powerful weapon in the Tombs of Amascut and will make a 500 run much easier, enabling tactics such as Butterfly Akkha, and doing enough damage to defeat Akkha's Shadows quickly or end Warden's enrage phase early. See Tombs of Amascut/Strategies for a breakdown of the best weapons for each encounter. The next best weapons for Wardens are the Twisted bow and Bow of Faerdhinen. An Osmumten's fang is all but required for Kephri and Ba-ba.
Since the Keris partisan of the sun is likely going to be your only form of healing due to 'Dehydration' and 'No help needed', the amount of Super restores you bring in will be the only supplies you will have access to for the entire raid.
(More on the wiki page of this task.)

Maybe I'm the boss. is a grandmaster combat achievement which requires the player to complete a Tombs of Amascut raid with every single boss invocation activated and without anyone dying.
Strategy:
All boss invocations must be activated to attempt this achievement. This includes invocations that are commonly considered annoying such as Medic!, Keep Back, and Double Trouble. Having all the invocations active will result in a raid level of 310. It is recommended to attempt this task in a group encounter, as Akkha's and Kephri's mechanics are easier to handle in a group. However, decently skilled player shouldn't have much trouble completing this in a solo encounter either.
Akkha is the largest threat in this achievement, as Double Trouble will result in Akkha using two special attacks at once. This is particularly problematic if this rolls into memory and orbs, as the orbs will not expire before the memory quadrants below path level 4. Akkha's other invocations are less of a threat, but by attempting in a group, players may instead get memory and detonation, which is far easier to handle. Player should also be familiar with how to deal with Keep Back invocation before attempting this task, especially if attempting solo.
(More on the wiki page of this task.)

Dropped the ball is an elite combat achievement which requires the player to defeat Akkha without dropping any materialising orbs and without dying, at raid level 150 or above.\nStrategy:\nThis refers to your character spawning the orbs from Akkha's special attack, not the white orbs on the final phase. Stand still during the shadow special to complete the task.

Akkhan't Do it is a grandmaster combat achievement which requires the player to defeat Akkha with all Akkha invocations activated and the path levelled up to at least four, without dying, at raid level 300 or above. Note that dying and resetting the fight allows multiple retries of this achievement.
Strategy:
Using the butterfly method is highly recommended for this method, since Akkha has to be fought with a raid level of 300 or higher.
In solo encounters, the player will have to handle both Memory Blast and Trailing Orbs at once, which when coupled with Akkha's level 4 path levelling results in six iterations of Memory Blast being used. Trailing Orbs can also prove to be daunting as the player will have less tiles to move around as it causes an orb to spawn in front of them after each movement, so players will need to run for the entirety of the attack; fortunately, at such a level, the trailing orbs will end around the fourth blast. Keep Back will also force the player to keep their distance from Akkha in his magic and ranged states, as a melee attack is also launched at the same time with them, which is further compounded by the fact that Akkha walks towards his target regardless of combat style.
Walk the Path is required to reach path level 4. In addition, the Pathmaster invocation is strongly recommended.
(More on the wiki page of this task.)

No skipping allowed is an elite combat achievement which requires the player to defeat Ba-Ba while only destroying uncracked boulders, without dying, and having the Boulderdash invocation active, at raid level 150 or above.
Strategy:
This achievement can be easily completed simultaneously along with I'm in a rush.
Create a 150 raid with Boulderdash active.
Prepare by dying repeatedly to farm ~25 honey locusts. This can be sped up with the help of a Locator orb or Dwarven rock cake. During the boulder phase, you will be tanking boulders in a corner of the room. There are seven boulders in each phase, so fourteen boulders will need to be tanked in total. Each boulder can deal 20 to 27 damage at 150 raid level. 27 damage x 14 boulders = 378 damage, 378/20 healing per Honey locust = ~19 Honey locusts to negate the incoming damage.
Survive both boulder phases by taking full damage, and you will receive both combat achievements.

I'm in a rush is an elite combat achievement which requires the player to defeat Ba-Ba after destroying four or fewer rolling boulders in total without dying, at raid level 150 or above.
Strategy:
This achievement can be easily completed simultaneously along with No skipping allowed.
Create a 150 raid (with Boulderdash active if completing along with No skipping allowed).
Prepare by dying repeatedly to farm ~25 honey locusts. This can be sped up with the help of a Locator orb or Dwarven rock cake. During boulder phase, you will be tanking boulders in a corner of the room. All of them. There are seven boulders in each phase, so fourteen boulders will need to be tanked in total. Each boulder can deal 20 to 27 damage at 150 raid level. 27 damage x 14 boulders = 378 damage, 378/20 healing per Honey locust = ~19 Honey locusts to negate the incoming damage.
Survive both boulder phases taking full damage and you will receive both combat achievements.

Ba-Bananza is a master combat achievement which requires the player to defeat Ba-Ba with all Ba-Ba invocations activated and the path levelled up to at least four, without dying.\nIn solo, task is awarded even with multiple deaths, so it is recommended to set invocations to unlimited deaths, so that you can try repeatedly. Set invocations Walk the path and Pathmaster to have a chance to get room to level 4 as the second path. An invocation level of 300 is required to achieve the task, so it is recommended to pick remaining invocations that will not make a difference to completing the task, such as those affecting the Wardens.\nIf still struggling, you can attempt the monkey room as the third boss (doing two easier ones first) allowing use for ambrosia given by helpful spirit. Double check the monkey path has levelled up to 4 before attempting, as Walk the path is random.

All Praise Zebak is a grandmaster combat achievement which requires the player to kill Zebak without losing prayer points at raid level 300 or above, while also satisfying the requirements of Rockin' around the croc achievement.
Strategy:
Along with meeting the aforementioned combat achievement, players must not lose a prayer point during the fight. Toggling the Deadly Prayers invocation off can help incase a mistake is made, as the heavy damage that would likely be inflicted from a mistake will result in disqualification.
Players may turn off Invocations that limit the number of attempts as previous deaths against Zebak during the same raid do not affect the task. It is recommended to attempt the achievement on a level 300 raid, with Pathmaster and Walk The Path active to force all bosses to a path level of 3. Then clear the Path of Scabaras, as it uses minimal supplies. There is a 33% chance for the Crondis' path to not level up, as it will be competing with both Apmeken and Het's paths; if this occurs, reset the raid until Crondis' path levels up. Alternatively, one can clear the Path of Apmeken next. The upside to doing so is gaining smelling salts for Zebak which can make the fight significantly easier.
(More on the wiki page of this task.)

Rockin' around the croc is a master combat achievement which requires the player to defeat Zebak at a path level of 4 with all invocations active without dying, at raid level 300 or above.
Strategy:
At a path level of 4, Zebak will attack every 5 ticks (every 3 seconds), increasing to 2 upon triggering the enrage phase (every 1.2 seconds). In addition, his Tidal Waves attack will now only have a single gap, although the waves can still be skipped over with proper experience.
In addition, the Pathmaster invocation is most direct way of levelling Zebak to the level 4 path requirement. It is however possible to get it with both Pathseeker or Pathfinder active - the probability of having Zebak reaching level 4 during such raids is 1/3, and 5/6 respectively.
In solo you can still get the achievement even after dying multiple times.

Doesn't bug me is a master combat achievement which requires the player to defeat Kephri with all invocations active, a path level of 4 and without dying at raid level 300 or above.
Strategy:
This achievement can be done solo, however the Medic! invocation is extremely annoying in solo and thus a small group of up to 4 players is recommended for this task, as to mitigate the impact of Aerial Assault.
Two players should trap the Soldier Scarab spawn that appears to the north centre so to prevent it from attacking the team. The Spitting Scarab should be attacked by two or three players while another player handles all the swarms that appear. In the second cycle, focus on the Arcane Scarab and then the Spitting one. The second soldier scarab can usually be ignored.
Try to combine this achievement with a raid level of 450 to try and get Remnant of Kephri at the same time.

All out of medics is a master combat achievement which requires the player to defeat Kephri without letting her heal above 25% after the first down, without dying, at raid level 300 or above. The 'Medic' invocation must be activated. Any healing from the Soldier Scarab will not fail this task.
Strategy::
Use Runelite's "Tombs of Amascut" Plugin, enable swarmer overlay under Kephri to see the spawn count. During the fight, healing swarms spawn every 15 ticks, Starting on the east side and rotating spawns clockwise until healing phase occurs. This allows for 2 fang hits immediately followed up by switching to Black chinchompa to clear the healing swarm.
Healing Phase 1:
28 swarms spawn in this phase, there are 18 swarm spawns that can heal kephri before the despawn timer expires. To stay under the 25% requirement, 16 must be cleared in time.
This is easiest to achieve in a 3-person group, where two people dedicate themselves to swarms, while a third focuses on kephri and the scarabs.
Healing Phase 2:
24 Healing swarms spawn, the first 14 must all be killed with a blowpipe.

Down Do Specs is an elite combat achievement which requires the player to defeat the Wardens after staggering the boss twice during phase 2 without dying, at raid level 150 or above.
Strategy:
This achievement is a reference to the two-cycle method used to finish the Wardens quickly. The player should have as much strength bonus as possible to maximise their melee hits. Make sure that you are under the effects of smelling salts to boost damage.
Keep one liquid adrenaline for this task. A lightbearer is not needed for lower raid levels, but is still helpful for reducing wait times. If on the Arceuus Spellbook, the spell Death Charge will restore energy when the core is returned to the Warden, as it counts as a "death" for the spell as long as the player has attacked the core at least once.
During the first cycle, dump five dragon dagger specials and follow up with a powerful two-handed weapon (e.g a godsword) as the final hit. On the second cycle, drink another dose of adrenaline (if the first one was used on the obelisk) and dump as many special attacks as possible - ideally having six or seven specials on hand should be enough for lower raid levels, followed with a 4-tick weapon (e.g whip). In group encounters, the overall damage is higher and should usually be enough to two cycle as long as each player's max hit is high enough.

Better get movin is a master combat achievement which requires the player to defeat Elidinis' Warden in phase three of the Wardens fight with 'Aerial Assault', 'Stay vigilant' and 'Insanity' invocations activated, and without dying, at raid level 150 or above.\nCompleting the raid with the specified invocations, without fighting the correct warden in phase three, still yields in success.

Confident Raider is a hard combat achievement which requires the player to complete a Tombs of Amascut raid at level 100 or above. Although this achievement is classified as an Entry Mode task, it can be completed in a Normal or Expert mode raid.

More than just a ranged weapon is a master combat achievement which requires the player to kill the Phantom Muspah via the use of salamanders.
Strategy:
All damage dealt must be by salamander, including the prayer shield phase (using corruption is allowed). The best salamander is the tecu salamander, which uses irit tar as ammunition. It is recommended to use the salamander in Ranged mode (Flare) during the Muspah's ranged phase, and in Magic mode (Blaze) during its melee phase, along with a full gear and prayer switches for each style. As freezes and thralls cannot be used, it is useful to instead bring the runes for greater corruption.
As the salamander's attack range is 1, players must use the step-back method during the Muspah's melee phase to avoid excessive damage. During the fight, try to ensure spikes are placed around the edges of the arena rather than in the center, otherwise the tiles around the Muspah may fill with spikes during the final phase and leave the player unable to attack. Greater corruption is invaluable for the prayer shield phase (Smite is more difficult to use than usual as salamanders' attack speed in Ranged mode is 4 while the Muspah's is 5).
Note: As the player can only deal damage with salamanders, any other types of damage such as thralls or recoil damage will automatically fail the achievement.

Can't Escape is an elite combat achievement which requires the player to kill the Phantom Muspah without running.
This achievement fails as soon as the player either leaves the starting tile with Run on, or turns Run on at any point during the fight. Only walking is permissible.
Strategy:
Using the step-back method will avoid all damage from the Muspah's melee attacks if properly timed. For players who are unable to do this, binding the muspah is also viable, though it will not remain bound for the full time.

Essence Farmer is a master combat achievement which requires the player to kill the Phantom Muspah 10 times in one trip.
Strategy:
Learning how to perform the stepback method can help conserve run energy and supplies whilst it is in its melee form. Try to deal as much damage as possible during the teleport attack, as some form changes can be skipped with sufficient damage, reducing the need for switching.
A potential strategy is to bring a range and mage setup with ancient magicks. Use range against Muspah when it is range phase and switch to mage for melee phase. Muspah is weak to magic during melee phase. It can be frozen with ice spells and you can heal using blood spells.
During the prayer shield phase, having access to multiple forms of prayer drain, such as smite and enchanted dragon sapphire bolts, will be helpful in removing it so the boss can be damaged faster, as the damage begins to increase at this point.
The muspah drops summer pies, sharks, super restores, and prayer potions to help with supplies, but don't rely on these fully for the ten kills needed.

Phantom Muspah Speed-Trialist is an elite combat achievement which requires the player to kill the Phantom Muspah in less than 3 minutes without a Slayer task.\nStrategy:\nFor strategies on this achievement, see Phantom Muspah Speed-Runner.

Phantom Muspah Speed-Chaser is a master combat achievement which requires the player to kill the Phantom Muspah in less than 2 minutes without being on a Slayer task.\nStrategy:\nFor strategies on this achievement, see Phantom Muspah Speed-Runner.

Phantom Muspah Speed-Runner is a grandmaster combat achievement which requires the player to kill the Phantom Muspah in less than 1 minute and 30 seconds without being on a Slayer task.
Strategy:
Having a twisted bow is essentially required for the task due to its high damage and accuracy against the Muspah. The tumeken's shadow will improve chances if bringing magic swaps, but the task is relatively reliably doable with only a twisted bow, as it still hits hard in the melee phase with good accuracy rolls. If opting to not use magic, vengeance during melee phase greatly improve odds. Ideally, the player should focus most of their damage when the Muspah uses its Lightning Cloud attack, as it will not change forms until the attack ends and thus minimise the time required switching gear.
Players lacking Zaryte crossbow should consider resetting until they start the fight with a successful dragon warhammer or elder maul special attack. Reducing the defence of the Muspah greatly increases the damage of the twisted bow, and the chance of a successful smite skip. Ring of shadows upgraded with the frozen tablet makes restoring the special attack easy.
(More on the wiki page of this task.)

Space is Tight is a master combat achievement which requires the player to kill the Phantom Muspah whilst it is surrounded by spikes.
Strategy:
All the tiles next to the Phantom Muspah, after the prayer shield phase, must be covered in spikes. Slowly navigate around it, while praying accordingly; spikes will emerge every four attacks and cover more tiles, growing from existing clusters of spikes. As such, the player should try to set up spikes during this phase in empty spots, as the clusters will eventually cover the tiles around the boss.
Players may also try to set up spikes during the kill, though it is much better to wait until the end of shield phase to do so due to the homing spikes mechanic possibly relocating them to less desirable spots.

Versatile Drainer is an elite combat achievement which requires the player to drain the Phantom Muspah's prayer with three different sources in one kill.
Strategy:
This can be accomplished by using any three of the following in a single fight:
- Enchanted sapphire bolts effect
- Ancient mace special attack (low chance of hitting even with melee gear)
- Attacking with the Smite prayer active
- Attacking with Corruption spells from the Arceuus spellbook

Walk Straight Pray True is a master combat achievement which requires the player to kill the Phantom Muspah without taking any avoidable damage during the fight.
Avoidable damage includes:
- Lightning Cloud damage
- Melee hits
- Spike spawn damage
- Spike walk-on damage
- Magic damage
- Off-prayer ranged hits
Does not include periodical chip damage through Ranged prayer.
For the magic attack, the player must pray against it before the attack is launched, or they will fail the achievement.

Phantom Muspah Manipulator is a grandmaster combat achievement which requires the player to kill the Phantom Muspah whilst also completing the Walk Straight Pray True, Space is Tight, and Can't Escape tasks in the same kill. This means the player must do the following:
- Have run energy turned off
- Surround the boss with spikes during the last phase
- Take no avoidable damage
Although the damage is calculated at the start of the projectile, not having Protect from Magic enabled when the corruption magic attack hits the player will still fail the combat achievement. Additionally, you will not get notified that you have failed this CA this way if you have "Combat Achievement Tasks - Failure" enabled.
You can utilise Ice ancient sceptre to freeze the boss during its melee phase.
Tip: You can walk through the Muspah in the final phase to easily place spikes wherever you want them, before going to a larger, more open area to finish it off once it is surrounded by spikes.

Vardorvis Speed-Trialist is an elite combat achievement which requires the player to kill Vardorvis in less than 1 minute and 15 seconds without a slayer task.\nStrategy:\nFor strategies on this achievement, see Vardorvis Speed-Runner.

Vardorvis Speed-Chaser is a master combat achievement which requires the player to kill Vardorvis in less than 1 minute and 5 seconds without a slayer task.\nStrategy:\nFor strategies on this achievement, see Vardorvis Speed-Runner.

Vardorvis Speed-Runner is a grandmaster combat achievement which requires the player to kill Vardorvis in less than 55 seconds without being on a slayer task.
Strategy:
Vardorvis has 700 hitpoints with a Defence level of 215.
Players may choose to start each kill by procing enchanted ruby bolts with a zaryte crossbow to deal 110 damage at the start of the kill.
Players should maximise their strength and slash bonus to ensure their attacks will hit, as Vardorvis has +65 slash defence bonus. Vardorvis' Defence will decrease by 1 for every 10 hitpoints missing. If the player can afford it, bringing a bellator ring for the start and ultor ring for later can help maximise damage. Use dragon claws around the ~250 hitpoints mark so they have the best chance of hitting. A voidwaker can be used to ignore accuracy checks, but may deal less damage than claws. A dose of surge potion can be used to restore 25% special attack energy, allowing the additional use of a burning claws special attack near the end of the fight.
An ironman or low budget alternative is using an Arkan blade instead of a voidwaker (requires completion of The Final Dawn). It has a maximum hit of over 80 with best-in-slot gear, only uses 30% special attack energy and is a 4-tick weapon. The burn effect will also stack up an additional 10 damage per spec that lands.
(More on the wiki page of this task.)

Vardorvis Sleeper is a grandmaster combat achievement which requires the player to kill awakened Vardorvis once.
Strategies:
Refer here for information about awakened Vardorvis.
Warning: The awakened Vardorvis is a significant step up compared to normal mode, and players should expect to die multiple times before securing an awakened Vardorvis kill. Each attempt will cost one Awakener's orb, costing each, so be mindful of this when attempting the achievement.

Perfect Vardorvis is a master combat achievement which requires the player to kill Vardorvis five times within the same instance, without taking any avoidable damage.
Avoidable damage includes:
- Damage from a melee attack off-prayer
- Damage from all special attacks
As the task's description implies, you must simply achieve 5 perfect kills in a single instance, rather than having to do so 5 kills in a row. This means that even if you achieve multiple perfect kills and fail before completing the task, you can continue to attempt perfect kills without leaving, provided you have sufficient supplies to do so.

Axe Enthusiast is a grandmaster combat achievement which requires the player to kill Vardorvis after surviving for 3 minutes during his enrage phase, whilst never leaving the central 25 tiles of the fight area.
Strategy:
Vardorvis will initiate the enrage phase upon reaching ~33% of his health (~231 health); it is recommended to position at the centre at 250 health to avoid failing the achievement. Saradomin brews are essentially mandatory for this achievement.
Once enrage starts, a set of axes will appear after the previous set has been thrown off the arena. It is recommended to stay by the edges of the arena, so that only one or two axes (if both axes are lined up together) will hit at a time. An axe will deal ~35 damage if Protect from Melee is not active, which is reduced by ~50% if the prayer was active. Since Vardorvis' Head will also attack more frequently, players will either need to flick the incoming projectile or tank an axe hit instead. The player will also likely get hit by Darting Spikes, since trying to avoid it may cause the player to clip an axe instead. Alternatively, the player can leave Vardorvis around 150 health, which will only cause two iterations of spikes which can be avoided by stepping one tile away, though care should be taken to avoid moving out of the zone.
The elysian spirit shield and staff of the dead can be used to mitigate damage.
(More on the wiki page of this task.)

Budget Cutter is a master combat achievement which requires the player to kill Vardorvis in combat equipment worth under .
Strategy:
The achievement requires both the player's Worn Equipment and inventory to be under . This includes food and potions but does not include the price of runes in a rune pouch. If the item is untradeable, its value will be used instead. Note that this is not the case for the Slayer helmet or imbued items; the value of its components will be used instead.
By opening the Items Kept on Death interface and selecting "PK Skull active", the player can see the total guide risk value of their setup; note that items with tradeable ornament kits or a Trouver parchment attached to it may increase its value without it being visible in the interface.
The game will not tell players whether they've failed the achievement, and will simply give no completion message upon killing Vardorvis, so checking that the total value is valid before starting the fight is recommended.
The player should use a fairly cheap, but strong slash-based weapon, such as a dragon scimitar or Saradomin sword.
Equipment:
As prices fluctuate, it may be worth using lower tier items to remain below .

Whisperer Speed-Trialist is an elite combat achievement which requires the player to kill the Whisperer in under 3 minutes without being on a slayer task.
Strategy:
Unlike Whisperer Speed-Chaser and Whisperer Speed-Runner, this achievement does not require the use of a Tumeken's shadow, but it does make it easier. Magic damage boosting equipment, such as ancestral robes, occult necklace, and the tormented bracelet is recommended. A magus ring is also useful but not required for the task. You can complete the achievement with other powered staves, such as a trident of the swamp, but it is less consistent and will require more attempts.
Knowing when to attack the Whisperer is helpful in dealing extra damage for the task, and a venator bow is highly recommended for the Lost Souls mechanic, as this will rebound 75 damage to her when the chant is fully disrupted.

Whisperer Speed-Chaser is a master combat achievement which requires the player to kill the Whisperer in less than 2 minutes and 25 seconds without being on a slayer task.\nStrategy:\nFor strategies on this achievement, see Whisperer Speed-Runner.

Whisperer Speed-Runner is a grandmaster combat achievement which requires the player to kill the Whisperer in less than 2 minutes and 5 seconds without being on a slayer task.
Strategy:
It is highly recommended to only attempt this achievement with a Tumeken's shadow and good magic damage gear, as the time limit is very strict and other staffs/spells deal significantly lower damage per second. It is also likely that the player will need to get several enchanted ruby bolt activations, since they can deal a hefty amount damage to the boss, despite the boss' moderately high ranged defence.
Other helpful tips for the achievement include:
- Double Vengeance on the melee attack; the Whisperer has a max hit of 42 with the melee attack, and whatever is inflicted as the first hit will always be dealt as the second, which can rebound reasonable damage at the boss. Double Vengeance can be done twice per attempt; pre-venge before the start of the kill, let the cooldown pass and use it again when running into melee distance.
- Attacking the boss whenever possible; while she takes ~66% less damage while using specials, players can get several hits in during them.
- Knowing when to attack the boss after she finishes a special attack.
- Going past special mechanic threshold triggers if possible while she is in the middle of an attack.

Whispered is a grandmaster combat achievement which requires the player to kill the awakened Whisperer once.
Strategies:
Refer here for information about the awakened Whisperer.
Warning: The awakened Whisperer is a significant step up compared to normal mode, and players should expect to die multiple times before securing an awakened Whisperer kill. Each attempt will cost one Awakener's orb, costing each, so be mindful of this when attempting the achievement.

Perfect Whisperer is a master combat achievement which requires the player to kill the Whisperer five times within the same instance, without taking any avoidable damage.
Avoidable damage includes:
- Any damage from her ranged, magic, and melee attacks. Only unprotected melee attacks will fail the achievement.
- Getting hit by her tentacles.
- Getting hit by her Screech attack.
- Getting hit by her Soul Siphon attack.
- Stepping on a dark green corrupted seed.
- Any corrupted seeds being hatched.
As the task's description implies, you must simply achieve 5 perfect kills in a single instance, rather than having to do so 5 kills in a row. This means that even if you achieve multiple perfect kills and fail before completing the task, you can continue to attempt perfect kills without leaving, providing that you have sufficient supplies to do so.

Tentacular is an elite combat achievement which requires the player to kill the Whisperer while on the Arceuus spellbook. You can complete this combat achievement with the Whisperer's awakened variant.
Strategy:
Unlike the other spells that bind a target, grasp spells will not guarantee a bind, even if the attack does not splash, unless the player uses Undead Grasp and has cast Mark of Darkness within the last 135-178 seconds, depending on the player's base Magic level. By using aether runes (alongside fire and blood runes), all runes required for casting Mark of Darkness, Undead Grasp, and Resurrect Greater Ghost can fit in the regular rune pouch. If the player has a divine rune pouch, using soul and cosmic runes in place of aether will save per cast.
Players may instead opt to be as far away as possible from the Whisperer's location after her special attack concludes. As per the image below, the tiles north/south from the red/violet tiles will always be safe from the Whisperer's melee attacks when she tries to move towards the player, making binding her unnecessary.
If the Whisperer is about to reach the player, activate Protect from Melee; while it will not fully block the attack, it will mitigate roughly 33% of it. The Whisperer's melee hits have a max hit of 42, and whatever she inflicts as the first hit will always be dealt as the second hit.
(More on the wiki page of this task.)

Dark Memories is a grandmaster combat achievement which requires the player to kill the Whisperer whilst spending less than six seconds in the Shadow Realm prior to her enrage phase.
Strategy:
The player must spend the bare minimum amount of time within the Shadow Realm:
- Shadow Leeches - The player can guess which corrupted seed without having to ever step foot inside the Shadow Realm. Stepping on the wrong seed will deal moderate damage, but the pattern can be easily determined after one mistake. Alternatively, the player can step on every corrupted seed while rapidly eating high healing food as stepping on the wrong seed does not drain sanity.
- Soul Siphon - The mechanic can be safely ignored; however, players will take 40 damage and lose 40% sanity in the process.
- Screech - Quickly observe the health of the pillars and then immediately leave, since trying to blindly guess the solution to this mechanic can be particularly dangerous.

Leviathan Speed-Trialist is an elite combat achievement which requires the player to kill the Leviathan in under 1 minute and 50 seconds, without being on a slayer task.\nStrategy:\nFor strategies on this achievement, see Leviathan Speed-Runner.

Leviathan Speed-Chaser is a master combat achievement which requires the player to kill the Leviathan in under 1 minute and 25 seconds, without being on a slayer task.\nStrategy:\nFor strategies on this achievement, see Leviathan Speed-Runner.

Leviathan Speed-Runner is a grandmaster combat achievement which requires the player to kill the Leviathan in less than 1 minute and 10 seconds, without being on a slayer task.
Strategy:
To make time, it is useful to aim for at least 4-5 Ruby dragon bolt (e) procs (ideally with a Zaryte crossbow for stronger procs) and large Vengeance rebounds. When leviathan's health reaches ~45%, use full Crystal armour with a Bow of Faerdhinen to get it down to enrage phase. As you proc enrage, switch into gear that strongly boosts max hits such as Elite Void Ranged or Masori armour. Use Webweaver bow special attack(s), then switch to a Toxic blowpipe to finish the kill.
Use Spellbook Swap in order to make use of both Thralls and Vengeance. The Leviathan only takes recoil damage from its melee attack, meaning the player must stand in melee distance and wait for the bite attack to trigger the recoil effect. Stunning will slow the kill down and is not neccessary. If you are on pace, Leviathan will reach enrage before it can ramp up to faster speeds; do not bring runes for shadow spells.
With Tumeken's shadow and strong mage gear, it is possible to hit over 110 after stunning The Leviathan. If planning to use this, ideally proc enrage with it.

Leviathan Sleeper is a grandmaster combat achievement which requires the player to kill the awakened Leviathan once.
Strategies:
Refer here for information about the awakened Leviathan.
Warning: The Awakened Leviathan is considered a significant step up compared to other Awakened bosses, especially during the enrage phase and players should expect to die multiple times before securing an awakened Leviathan kill. Each attempt will cost one Awakener's orb, costing each, so be mindful of this when attempting the achievement.

Perfect Leviathan is a master combat achievement which requires the player to kill the Leviathan five times without leaving and taking any avoidable damage.
Avoidable damage includes:
- Standard rapid-fire volleys
- Getting hit by falling debris during and outside of enrage phase
- Bite damage
- Lightning Barrage damage
- Smoke Blast damage (avoiding boulders and the blast itself)
- Prayer-piercing damage during the enrage phase from being outside the range of the abyssal pathfinder
Note: Taking damage from one of the rapid-fire volleys during the transition to the enrage phase—while praying the correct style—will not disqualify the player from a 'perfect' kill. During the enrage phase, however, standing outside the abyssal pathfinder's area and taking this damage will disqualify the player, regardless of whether the correct protection prayer is active.
As the task's description implies, you must simply achieve 5 perfect kills in a single instance, rather than having to do so 5 kills in a row. This means that even if you achieve multiple perfect kills and fail before completing the task, you can continue to attempt perfect kills without leaving, providing that you have sufficient supplies to do so.

Serpentine Solo is a master combat achievement which requires the player to kill the Leviathan without stunning it more than once with shadow spells.
Strategy:
With full crystal armour and a Bow of Faerdhinen, the player should be able to deal a good amount of damage, alternatively, a zaryte crossbow with enchanted ruby bolts and a little luck can also work.
At the end of each volley, the boss will roar and cause debris to fall around the arena, with one falling down on the player's location as a permanent spawn for the remainder of the fight. Players will take minor unavoidable damage from the roar, but can avoid the debris by moving away from where they stood. Every subsequent volley of attacks will increase in intensity, which can make it difficult to switch prayers at later volleys. The sequence of attacks are as follows:
- 3 tick attacks with magic and ranged
- 2 tick attacks with magic and ranged
- 2 tick attacks with all three styles
- 1 tick attacks with magic and ranged
- 1 tick attacks with all three styles
- All three styles with faster projectile time (2 ticks to react)
- All three styles with even faster projectile time (1 tick to react)
The player should be able to comfortably handle at least the first five attack speeds without much issue before stunning the boss. When the boss has lost 25% of its health or is stunned, its attack speed will decrease.
(More on the wiki page of this task.)

Unconventional is a grandmaster combat achievement which requires the player to kill the Leviathan using only mithril ammunition whilst having no more than 25 Hitpoints throughout the entire fight.
Strategy:
Bring a self-damaging item (such as a locator orb or dwarven rock cake) to quickly bring your health down before starting a fight. Bring yourself down to 30-35 health, then drink a dose of divine ranging or bastion potion to reach the required threshold. The task also effectively requires performing a perfect kill, as getting hit by anything will almost surely result in death.
Due to the low damage output of mithril ammunition, the player should expect a longer-than-average kill at the boss. Possible options include using the toxic blowpipe with mithril darts, zaryte crossbow alongside enchanted emerald bolts, a twisted bow with seeking mithril arrows; despite the Leviathan's less-than-optimal Magic level of 160, the latter option with best-in-slot Ranged gear and Rigour has a max hit of 49. A magic shortbow (i) can be used for its special attack inside the abyssal pathfinder. Thralls can be used for this task.
NOTE: Rosewood, ironwood, and camphor blowpipes with mithril darts currently cause the player to fail the combat achievement upon use, despite being mithril ammunition.
(More on the wiki page of this task.)

Duke Sucellus Speed-Trialist is an elite combat achievement which requires the player to kill Duke Sucellus in under 1 minute, without a slayer task.\nStrategy:\nFor strategies on this achievement, see Duke Sucellus Speed-Runner.

Duke Sucellus Speed-Chaser is a master combat achievement which requires the player to kill Duke Sucellus in under 50 seconds, without a slayer task.
Despite the task saying "under 50 seconds," a time of 0:50:40 will still complete the task.
Strategy:
For strategies on this achievement, see Duke Sucellus Speed-Runner.

Duke Sucellus Speed-Runner is a grandmaster combat achievement which requires the player to kill Duke Sucellus in less than 40 seconds, without being on a slayer task.
Strategy:
The kill time for the Duke speed tasks starts as soon as Sucellus wakes up, which does not include the preparation phase.
In order to meet the requirements for this task, the player will need a strong slash weapon, ideally the Scythe of Vitur, to take advantage of Sucellus' weakness to slash and the potential to hit harder than any other slash weapon. Make sure to cast Vengeance before the kill starts, then spellbook swap to the Arceuus spellbook and summon a melee thrall.
As Sucellus has a fairly high Defence level of 275, the player can hope for a high-hitting Bandos godsword special to lower his Defence to a more reasonable level. A surge potion allows for an additional burning claws special within the time frame; use it directly after the Bandos godsword special to let the burn deal damage over time. Sucellus' magic attack maxes 48 and his melee 56; so a good chunk of damage can be reflected back. Attack Duke, step back to tank an off prayer mage attack, cast another Vengeance, attack Sucellus, and get hit by his melee attack. As this has the potential to kill the player, pre-eating an anglerfish to 121 health can be beneficial.
(More on the wiki page of this task.)

Duke Sucellus Sleeper is a grandmaster combat achievement which requires the player to kill awakened Duke Sucellus once.
Strategies:
Refer here for information about the awakened Sucellus.
Warning: The awakened Sucellus is a significant step up compared to normal mode, and players should expect to die multiple times before securing an awakened Sucellus kill. Each attempt will cost one Awakener's orb, costing each, so be mindful of this when attempting the achievement.

Perfect Duke Sucellus is a master combat achievement which requires the player to kill Duke Sucellus five times within the same instance, without taking any avoidable damage.
Avoidable damage includes:
- Melee attacks from his slam attack (the chip damage taken from the rising icicles are considered unavoidable)
- Standard magic attack (praying against them will still fail the achievement, even when hit for a 0)
- Damage from the Freezing Gaze attack
- Damage from ignited gas vents in both the preparation and battle phases
- Damage from ice fall and extremities
As the task's description implies, you must simply achieve 5 perfect kills in a single instance, rather than having to do so 5 kills in a row. This means that even if you achieve multiple perfect kills and fail before completing the task, you can continue to attempt perfect kills without leaving, providing that you have sufficient supplies to do so.

Cold Feet is a master combat achievement which requires the player to kill Duke Sucellus while walking and taking zero avoidable damage.
Strategy:
Players must not run for the entire duration of the fight, including the potion preparation portion, making it similar to Perfect Duke Sucellus, except the player has to walk for one kill. Even when walking, many of Sucellus' attacks are very easy to avoid. The only main issue for this achievement is the gas flares attack. Each gas flare will launch at the vent the player is closest to, which has a 3x3 AoE from the vent tile. If the player walks the wrong direction, they will take damage from the resulting gas. For a detailed description of when the gas flare attack occurs, see the strategy guide.
Although the Speed Running Achievements were updated to only include the time from when Duke wakes up, this Achievement still fails if you take damage during the preparation phase. The preparation phase isn't required for the achievement, however, as you are able to prepare poison for multiple kills at once, and achievement eligibility resets after killing Duke.

Mirror Image is a grandmaster combat achievement which requires the player to kill Duke Sucellus whilst only attacking the boss on the same tick that he attacks the player.
Strategy:
For this achievement, the player will need to attack on the same tick that Duke Sucellus initiates an attack. He attacks on a five-tick cycle (3.0s) until enrage at 25% health (121 or less health), in which he attacks on a four-tick cycle (2.4s). Therefore, the player should use a five-tick weapon (e.g a Scythe of Vitur) pre-enrage, then swap to a four-tick weapon (ideally Emberlight) during enrage to match Duke Sucellus' attacks. The player should also avoid attacking during Gas Flares as to not mess up the attack cycle, since he launches gas faster than his auto-attacks.
Alternatively, players may also choose to never directly attack Duke Sucellus, and solely kill him through recoil-induced damage, such is possible with: the ring of suffering (r)/ring of recoil, Echo boots, Vengeance, and a Dharok 's set (with an amulet of the damned). Players should turn off Protect from Melee, then cast Vengeance right before the slamming part of his melee attack to effectively rebound the damage, then hide by the pillars and avoid Gas Flares as usual until Vengeance can be cast again.
(More on the wiki page of this task.)

Perfect Scurrius is a medium combat achievement which requires the player to kill Scurrius in a private instance without taking damage from his Tail Swipe and Falling Bricks attacks, whilst praying correctly against his ranged and magic attacks.
Strategy:
Players should always have Protect from Melee active, or a way to bind Scurrius repeatedly to dodge his Tail Swipe. The Falling Bricks attack gives ample warning to dodge, and his magic and ranged attacks will only deal damage on impact, so players can pray against them even after the projectile is launched.
Using ranged or magic allows players to stand further away from the rat king, reducing the chance of an off-prayer melee hit.

Efficient Pest Control is a medium combat achievement which requires the player to kill six giant rats in Scurrius' lair in 3 seconds.
Strategy:
While the achievement states that it must be done in 3 seconds, the timer starts after the first rat kill, allowing for the use of a rat bone weapon to kill all six rats within the time frame. When using the Bone shortbow or Bone staff, it is recommended to attack the rats from furthest to nearest due to the projectile travel time.
Another method is letting the rats gather around Scurrius, and then using Dinh's bulwark's special attack on Scurrius.
An affordable alternative approach is to kill Scurrius, then use 2 rune thrownaxe specials back to back on the giant rats.

The Clone Zone is a hard combat achievement which requires the player to defeat the Eclipse Moon without damaging her outside of her clone attack.\nStrategy:\nAs the player can only attack during her clone special attack, players may have to take multiple phases of her attacks to complete the achievement. As such, a slow, high-hitting weapon is recommended to deal the most damage each phase. Also: recoil effects, such as from the Ring of suffering (ri), will not void the achievement and can safely be used between clone phases.

High Hitter is an elite combat achievement which requires the player to defeat a Moon before they start their second special attack.\nThis combat achievement does not count special attacks that are happening as you enter the room, so players struggling with this task may wish to enter shortly after a special starts, to give them more time.

Perilous Champion is a hard combat achievement which requires the player to open the Lunar Chest 25 times in the Moons of Peril.\nIf you are solely farming the combat achievement, defeating Eclipse Moon is a quick method of completing it. After defeating Eclipse Moon, you will be teleported into the Blue Moon area with the salamander sites. Run past the salamander sites to the far south-east entrance. Then continue running past the Blood Moon chamber entrance and take a sip of tea from the cooking stove on the way to the far south entrance. Collect your loot from the lunar chest then keep running north back to the Eclipse Moon chamber and repeat the process.

Perilous Dancer is a hard combat achievement which requires the player to defeat all the Moons of Peril in one run, while only taking damage from regular attacks.
Strategy:
Players must avoid damage from all special attacks of the bosses, such as the Frost Storms of the Blue Moon and the Searing Rays of the Eclipse Moon.
Being attacked outside of Eyatlalli's glyphs will fail the achievement.
The initial damage taken from the jaguar special attack that the Blood Moon uses will not fail this task, however, taking a hit from the jaguars themselves will.
The achievement is awarded after defeating the final Moon.
If you fail the combat achievement, you MUST reset the encounter by looting the reward chest to properly receive fail and success messages on following attempts.
Eclipse Moon:
Entering the arena during the Clones phase is advantageous to avoid being hit by the Searing Rays.
You can avoid the Searing Rays altogether by entering when the second south-western glyph begins to glow, and killing the boss before the second special attack begins. Recommended for players that lack the equipment to kill the boss quickly.
Bringing a godsword or better, to quickly damage the boss during the Clones phase, is highly recommended.
Blue Moon:
Enter during the Frost Storm phase and wait on the south-western glyph for the next round to begin.
(More on the wiki page of this task.)

Fortified is a hard combat achievement which requires the player to defeat a Moon without consuming any supplies.\nStrategy:\nThe Blue Moon's special attacks are not particularly dangerous, and receives the most extra damage from multi-hit special attacks, such as the Dragon dagger. Make sure you drink a Moonlight or combat potion and are full HP prior to entering the arena.

Betrayal is a hard combat achievement which requires the player to defeat a Moon using the associated weapon.\nStrategy:\nPlayers must wear the matching weapon of the boss: the dual macuahuitl for the Blood Moon, the Eclipse atlatl for the Eclipse Moon, or the Blue Moon spear for the Blue Moon, to defeat them. The Blue Moon can be easily killed for this achievement, as the Blue Moon spear can be set to Crush and the boss' flat armour stat is -5. Alternatively, the weapon can be equipped just before the boss' death, as it does not need to be equipped for the entire fight for the achievement to count.

Back to Our Roots is a medium combat achievement which requires the player to defeat all three Moons of Peril with a dragon scimitar without leaving Neypotzli.
Strategy:
Aside from the weapon slot, the achievement can be completed whilst wearing other equipment; using thralls will not fail the achievement, either. The dragon scimitar (or) also counts for this achievement.
For accounts wishing to avoid gaining combat experience, this combat achievement can be completed without a dragon scimitar if the bosses are defeated exclusively with recoil damage.

Moons of Peril Speed-Trialist is a medium combat achievement which requires the player to defeat all three Moons of Peril in one run in under 8 minutes.\nThe timer begins upon entering the first boss room (the area where players use the statue to enter the boss arena). Importantly, this means supplies collection before fighting the first Moon does not count towards the timer.

Moons of Peril Speed-Chaser is a hard combat achievement which requires the player to defeat all three Moons of Peril in one run in under 6 minutes.\nThe timer begins upon entering the first boss room (the area where players use the statue to enter the boss arena). Importantly, this means supplies collection before fighting the first Moon does not count towards the timer.

Fat of the Land is a hard combat achievement which requires the player to defeat 30 Moons of Peril without leaving Neypotzli.\nStrategy:\nEach Moon will count once towards the achievement, rather than each opening of the Lunar Chest. As such, players performing a full run of each boss will need to do so a minimum of ten times. Additionally, progress is not lost upon logging out.

I Brought Mine Too is a master combat achievement which requires the player to defeat Sol Heredit using any spear, hasta, or halberd.
Strategy:
The noxious halberd is the most powerful weapon for this achievement, but its extra reach can prove difficult to use while dodging Sol's attacks if Myopia was not selected in the prior waves. The next best weapon is the Zamorakian hasta on slash with a defender. The dragon halberd is the best weapon for account builds who do not wish to gain defence XP and also who do not have 80 Attack. A dragon hunter lance may be used as well, though it is slightly worse than the Zamorakian hasta.
The only usable weapons that feature special attacks for this task are the crystal halberd, dragon halberd, and dragon hasta.

Slow Dancing in the Sand is a grandmaster combat achievement which requires the player to defeat Sol Heredit without running during the fight.
Strategy:
The player can easily avoid three of Sol's attacks by walking away one tile; the only problem will be his second shield bash, as this requires the player to be at least two tiles away from him to avoid getting hit.
With some luck and supplies, one may successfully tank the second shield bash throughout the fight. It is also possible to "pre-move" following a first shield bash to cover for the possibility that the next attack will be a second shield bash. The player must walk one tile away from Sol at the same time as he starts the animation for the second attack. This will result in Sol staying in place and the player reaching a position where they can escape a second shield bash in time without running.

Perfect Footwork is a grandmaster combat achievement which requires the player to defeat Sol Heredit without taking any damage from his Spear, Shield, Grapple, or Triple Attack.\nStrategy:\nThe player is allowed to be damaged by anything that is not one of Sol's attacks, so it is possible to step on molten sand or solar flares temporarily if needed to dodge an attack.

Showboating is a master combat achievement which requires the player to use the Fortis Salute emote to the north, east, south, and west of the arena while Sol Heredit is below 10% of his hitpoints.
Strategy:
Performing the emote while facing north, south, east, or west while Sol Heredit is below 10% health will cause a chat message "" to be displayed, confirming that the direction has been saluted towards. The message will not appear if the player is facing diagonally, and the player does not need to be at the edges of the arena to salute in a direction.
Fortis Salute is unlocked upon reaching 20,000 Glory.

Denied is an elite combat achievement which requires the player to complete wave 7 without the minotaur ever healing other enemies.
Strategy:
A minotaur will spawn 40 seconds into the wave. This wave will also include a Fremennik Warband (one archer, berserker and seer), a manticore, javelin colossus and a shockwave colossus. If the Quartet and/or Dynamic Duo handicaps are active, this will include an additional warbander and shockwave colossus.
The minotaur will heal enemies within a six tile radius from its centre tile only if it is not attacking the player. Ideally, the minotaur should spawn to the north and walk south-west towards the north-western pillar's upper area.
Once the wave starts, immediately kill the warband. If something spawns to the south, they can be lured to the bottom of the north-west pillar. The minotaur will not be able to heal any large enemies as long as it is positioned north of said pillar. Do not attack any enemies east of the north-west pillar, as they will be healed by the minotaur if not killed off.

One-off is a master combat achievement which requires the player to complete wave 11 of the Fortis Colosseum with either the 'Red Flag', 'Dynamic Duo', or 'Doom II' handicaps active.
Strategy:
Of the three, Dynamic Duo is the least dangerous option, since mages are the easiest mobs to deal with overall. Red Flag will result in the minotaur being able to path around pillars and prevent it from being safespotted, while Doom II removes the ability to recover from mistakes with brews.
Wave 11 consists of a Fremennik warband, one Javelin Colossus, one Shockwave Colossus (two if Dynamic Duo), two manticores along with a minotaur and serpent shaman as reinforcements.

Reinforcements is a grandmaster combat achievement which requires the player to defeat Sol Heredit with Bees II, Solarflare II and Quartet modifiers active.
Strategy:
Quartet causes a single Fremennik warbander to appear at the start of the wave, while Bees II will spawn two sets of bees that slowly home on the player. The bees will persist throughout the entire fight, so killing them off is mandatory, ideally with a scythe to avoid unnecessary swaps. Solarflare II is less of an issue if the player knows where to avoid standing. Any antipoison is highly recommended to lower damage from Bee Swarms.
Solarflare III and/or Bees III may also be taken for this task, but the latter should only be taken if it is the least harmful of the offered handicaps.
When aiming to complete this combat achievement, it's recommended to always take Solarflare I/II when available (optionally taking Solarflare III to remove it from the pool and increase the chances of seeing the other required modifiers). Quartet should be avoided until after wave 6, as having to kill an additional Fremennik significantly increases the chances of reinforcements spawning before south spawns are dealt with. Bees should generally be avoided until later waves as well, but can be taken earlier if using a venator bow to kill them passively, or if intending to use Saradomin godsword special attacks on them.

I was here first! is an elite combat achievement which requires the player to kill a jaguar warrior using a claw-type weapon special attack.\nStrategy:\nSuitable weapons for this include the rune claws, burning claws, and dragon claws, however the latter is much more consistent and harder-hitting. Make sure to have Protect from Melee enabled to prevent the jaguar warrior from damaging the player.

Colosseum Speed-Chaser is a master combat achievement which requires the player to complete the Fortis Colosseum with a total time of 28 minutes or less.\nStrategy:\nFor strategies on this achievement, see Colosseum Speed-Runner.

Colosseum Speed-Runner is a grandmaster combat achievement which requires the player to complete the Fortis Colosseum with a total time of 24 minutes or less.
Strategy:
Compared to the other Grandmaster speedrun times, this is an extremely lenient time to achieve. Gear does not matter very much, as any megarare setup or even an Osmumten's fang and venator bow in Bandos-tier gear can clear this threshold comfortably.
The biggest time saves in the Colosseum are:
- Learning to solve waves and stacks quickly - not running pillars too often (anything more than once or twice per KC is too much), not taking too long to set up pillar stack offticks, etc.
- Minimising tick loss, especially at the start of the wave.
- Using the venator bow for double bounce DPS in early waves; for this time threshold, you can just focus on using it on the reinforcements in early waves. This video and this imgur album show some common venator bow setups.
More difficult strategies, such as setting up difficult melee offticks or hitting the pillar stack before south spawns, are also helpful. However, the time can easily be achieved by focusing on quick solves, staying at high combat stats, and minimising tick loss.

Unending Torment is an elite combat achievement which requires the player to kill a Tormented Demon.
This achievement will only count as completed for Tormented Demons killed after the completion of While Guthix Sleeps. The two Tormented Demons killed during the quest while player's stats are temporarily increased due to touching the Stone of Jas do not count towards task completion.
Strategy:
Be familiar with the mechanics of Tormented Demons, which can pray against every combat style, and will attack using every combat style.
The Tormented Demons have a shield that reduces damage done by non-demonbane weapons by (25% or 33% needs confirmation). The Tormented Demon will drop his shield right after the special attack (where it snares the player and releases two bombs) for one auto attack. It is recommended to dump your non-demonbane special attack during this time-frame.
Every time a Tormented Demon loses 25% of its health since its last prayer swap, it will change overhead prayer to protection from whatever the last style of attack damaged it. When the Tormented Demon changes overhead prayer, it will stop attacking for 6 ticks (3.6s). Thralls can be used advantageously (using a third style) for this mechanic.
(More on the wiki page of this task.)

Two Times the Torment is an elite combat achievement which requires the player to kill two Tormented Demons within two seconds.
Strategy:
There are many places where players can fight two demons at a time; the large dolmen area and the eastern offshoots of the temple grounds. The player may also attempt this in a triples demon area if they choose to.
If completing this task without relying on venom, find two demons praying against the same combat style. This will help minimise the need to swap weapons. Bringing a heavy crush weapon and a heavy ranged weapon are recommended to minimise time needed finding the demons to set up the task.
If using a heavy melee weapon (dharok's greataxe, dragon 2h sword), find two demons that spawn with Protect from Melee. If using a ballista, find two demons that spawn with Protect from Missiles.
When fighting two demons at once, one will use magic or ranged, while the other will use melee. If the melee-using demon cannot use melee, it will use the style opposite of what the other demon is using. The demons will swap combat styles when they launch their binding projectile and fireball attack, which is done simultaneously. While the demons will usually attack off-tick to allow the player to flick the attack, it is possible for them to attack on-tick when they swap prayers. If this occurs, move around to make the melee demon's attacks off-tick.
(More on the wiki page of this task.)

Three Times the Thrashing is a master combat achievement which requires the player to kill three Tormented Demons within three seconds.
Strategy:
There are two spots where the player can fight three demons at a time, both of which are in the south-western corner of the temple. These chambers are fairly open in a straight line, though the eastern chamber of the two has a small funnel that can help obscure vision.
Fighting three demons at a time will result in one demon using ranged or magic, the second one using melee, and the third one attacking the player with a single 1x1 fireball attack. If the second demon cannot use melee, it will begin using ranged or magic (depending on what the first demon is using) until they run back into range.
It is recommended to bring plenty of Saradomin brews for the achievement, as the demons can hit very hard and accurately.
Precise venom method:
This method is slow, reliable, and requires lots of food. Set up the Tormented Demons by attacking each one until they are not praying from ranged.
Bring a death stack of a full inventory of Saradomin brews and die. Then bring another death stack of anglerfish and Saradomin brews, then die.
Bring a toxic blowpipe and serpentine helm for a guaranteed venom proc, as well as your best tank gear, such as Justiciar armour with Dinh's bulwark.
(More on the wiki page of this task.)

Rapid Reload is an elite combat achievement which requires the player to hit three tormented demons within three seconds using a ballista or crossbow.
Strategy:
The simplest way to complete this achievement is to use the Hunters' crossbow or Hunters' sunlight crossbow set to rapid attack style. Stand near three demons, and attack them each in succession starting from the one furthest from you (it must be at max distance or further). Their prayers and shields are irrelevant for this method.
The likely intended way to complete this achievement is to use the tormented demon's unique mechanics to gain attack speed bonuses. To complete this achievement using these mechanics, the player must engage three demons at once and hit them in rapid succession after they've dropped their fire shields. There are two triple-combat zones where the player can attempt the achievement, both of which are in the south-west section of the temple.
One way to set up the demons is to use a blowpipe set to rapid attack style to engage three unoccupied demons before proceeding to attack them all with a crossbow or ballista after their fire shield animation has played. Attack them each in succession starting from the one furthest from you for the best chance of success (due to the longer travel time of the missiles).
Araxxor Speed-Trialist is an elite combat achievement which requires the player to kill Araxxor 4 times within 10 minutes.\nStrategy:\nFor strategies on this achievement, see Araxxor Speed-Runner.
Araxxor Speed-Chaser is a master combat achievement which requires the player to kill Araxxor 5 times within 10 minutes.\nStrategy:\nFor strategies on this achievement, see Araxxor Speed-Runner.

Araxxor Speed-Runner is a grandmaster combat achievement which requires the player to kill Araxxor 6 times within ten minutes. This task includes Araxxor's respawn time (9 seconds), thus essentially requiring an average time of 1:31 or less for each kill.
Strategy:
Using strong gear (ideally near or fully best-in-slot, such as Inquisitor's armour, an inquisitor's mace or scythe of Vitur), damaging Araxxor using Ruptura Araxytes, and utilising the step-under method during his enrage phase will all help achieve the kill times needed for the achievement.
Players may also choose to leave mirrorback and Acidic Araxytes alive, rather than taking any time to kill them, especially because any extraneous damage taken can be healed while Araxxor respawns.

Perfect Araxxor is a master combat achievement requiring the player to perfectly kill Araxxor.
Strategy:
The task requires the player to achieve one kill without taking any avoidable damage, which includes:
- Damage off-prayer from Araxxor. For his magic attack, players are not disqualified if the resulting hit is 0, but this still requires having Protect from Magic activated.
- Damage off-prayer from acidic and mirrorback araxytes. A hit of 0 without the proper protection prayer activated will still disqualify players.
- Damage from stepping into acid pools
- Damage from being in the trajectory of Araxxor's Acid Ball
- Damage from a ruptura araxyte's explosion
- Reflected damage from mirrorback araxytes
Avoiding hits from acidic araxytes can be done by killing them with a single attack as soon as they spawn. Alternatively, for players without access to ballistae, all of the green eggs can be destroyed at the start of the fight, preventing the acidic araxytes from spawning. Even accounting for the delay when using a ranged weapon, the araxyte will not have time to attack the player if done fast enough. This allows the player to keep Protect from Melee on at all times throughout the fight.
It may also be beneficial to wait for Araxxor to begin the fight with a white or green egg, as the trajectories of the resulting acid pools can be predicted.

Perfect Araxxor 2 is a grandmaster combat achievement requiring the player to perfectly kill Araxxor as well as never hitting him during his enrage phase.
Note: The failure message for Perfect Araxxor 2 will not appear if the player fails the conditions of Perfect Araxxor prior to the enrage phase. It is recommended to enable the repeat failure message for Combat Achievements in the settings interface to know if Perfect Araxxor was failed, which automatically disqualifies the player from Perfect Araxxor 2.
Strategy:
This task mandates using the step-under method during Araxxor's enrage phase, which starts when his health falls below 255. It is recommended to lure him towards an area with a minimal amount of acid pools before having him enter his enrage phase to maximise the available space for the step-under method. Do not use burning claws or thralls, as the extra hits they deal after enrage will fail the task. Attacking Araxxor during enrage, even if it hits a 0, will automatically fail the task. If the player is concerned about hitting him by accident, equipping an ammo-using bow while having no ammo will prevent this from occurring, since the player would not be able to launch an attack without ammo.
(More on the wiki page of this task.)

Let it seep in is a master combat achievement which requires the player to kill Araxxor without ever having venom immunity. Despite the task's description, poison immunity will not disqualify the player from completing the achievement.
Strategy:
Venom damage is dealt every 18 seconds, starting at 6 and increasing by 2 every time it hits. Players proficient with the boss should be able to achieve one kill without drinking anti-venom with a standard inventory for a trip.
Players can also use the following methods to cure themselves without immunity being provided:
- Cure Me - one cast converts venom to poison, two casts fully cures the player.
- Guthix Rest - converts venom to poison, and heals 5 health per dose. It does not fully cure poison, it only reduces poison damage by 1. Drink when you see the first venom hit after being envenomed.
- Cooked moonlight antelope - converts venom to poison 7 ticks (4.2 seconds) after being eaten. Can be used alongside Cure Me to make the task easier.
- Noxious halberd - special attack cures venom and also deals the player's max hit against the hatched eggs.

Relaxxor is an elite combat achievement which requires the player to kill Araxxor after destroying six eggs.
Strategy:
It is recommended to first destroy the mirrorback araxyte eggs, as they are the most difficult to deal with among the three eggs. Players may allow the ruptura araxyte eggs to hatch if they are comfortable with luring it to Araxxor. If Araxxor tried to spawn an egg before you destroy it, then it does not count towards the 6 required eggs.
Another method is to simply attack the eggs in reverse order, going counter-clockwise. This allows you to fully destroy the eggs before they are attempted to spawn.

Swimming in Venom is a grandmaster combat achievement requiring the player to kill Araxxor without having him move.
Strategy:
Players are advised to bring a heavy ranged weapon (ideally a heavy ballista and dragon javelins with Rigour), as killing the Mirrorback Araxyte early on will reduce a large amount of recoil damage that would otherwise be incurred. This can also be used against Acidic Araxytes if the player does not want to handle flicking them, as they may end up in a position where they will attack in sync with Araxxor from the centre of the arena. Ruptura Araxytes can be easily ignored.
It is highly recommended that this achievement be attempted with a green egg starter, as this will result in Araxxor using Acid Ball - this attack is launched in one of eight directions depending on where Araxxor is facing, and players can manipulate it so that Araxxor will only launch the ball towards one direction. The acid generated by the ball is also lower, with only one tile ragged at most, as the resulting splatter will harmlessly land around the edges of the arena.
During the enrage phase, the player is highly encouraged to use the step-under method in order to prevent Araxxor from moving. This is especially important if the player does not have a good crush weapon, as space could be severely limited. With good gear and few ragged tiles, the step-under method can be optional.

Araxyte Betrayal is a master combat achievement which requires the player to have an araxyte kill three other araxytes.
Strategy:
The fastest way to get the achievement is to clump two Acidic Araxytes with another araxyte of the player's choosing - a Mirrorback Araxyte or even Araxxor himself, and then have a Ruptura Araxyte handle them. It is recommended to leave the acidic araxytes around ~40 or so hitpoints and Araxxor ~60 or so hitpoints so that the explosion will kill them in the event of improper luring; the Ruptura araxyte will deal 80 damage to anything underneath its tiles and 64 to anything next to it.
Araxxor's cleave attack during the enrage phase can also work, but this is much less efficient due to the hit tiles and the araxytes potentially moving out of the way.

Arachnid Lover is a master combat achievement requiring the player to kill Araxxor 10 times without leaving his lair.
Strategy:
Bringing Saradomin brews and super restores instead of hard food is advised for this task; though Araxxor has a 1/8 chance of dropping supplies, don't plan to rely on these fully for completing the task.
Alternatively, using a Saradomin godsword alongside a single defence reducing special attack, Lightbearer, and Death Charge will provide a large amount of Hitpoints/Prayer sustain for the player which should make it easily achievable if the supply drop is rolled.
Speed up kills by luring ruptura araxytes and utilising the step-under method during Araxxor's enrage phase to reduce his overall damage output.

Hueycoatl Veteran is an elite combat achievement which requires the player to kill The Hueycoatl 25 times.\nStrategy:\nPlayers wanting to increment their kill count quickly are recommended to do so on world 340 or 517, which are designated by the game as a "Varlamore PvM" world and are the likeliest worlds where masses of players are fighting the boss.

Perfect Hueycoatl is an elite combat achievement which requires the player to kill the Hueycoatl perfectly 5 times without leaving. Only the player seeking the achievement must get a perfect kill; other players in the fight do not need to.
Strategy:
The task requires the player to achieve five kills without taking any avoidable damage, which includes:
- Damage off-prayer from projectiles
- Damage from lightning strikes
- Damage from tail shockwaves
Additionally, as the task's description implies, you must simply achieve 5 perfect kills without leaving via the slope or chain, rather than having to do so 5 kills in a row. This means that even if you achieve multiple perfect kills and fail before completing the task, you can continue to attempt perfect kills without leaving, providing that you have sufficient supplies to do so. You may attempt to leave in order to check your current streak.
